chapters.title: Chapter 315 -315-Harsh Conditions, Prolonged Torture
paragraphs: Harris was a descendant of the Starlight Folk.

The Starbeast race was known as the greatest race in the Endless Starsea. In their youth, they would already reach supreme-grade. Once they became adults and awakened a portion of their bloodline, they could step into Divine-grade!
If they could awaken their entire bloodline and receive the complete inheritance, they would directly step into Oracle-grade as supreme-grade existences.
The innate gifts of this race could be described as unparalleled.
And in Daniel’s hands, there was currently a Starbeast egg!
"A puppet avatar has an upper limit of Divine-grade."
Daniel pondered. "Therefore, I need a top-grade avatar."

"With the racial Fortune Points and supreme talent of the starry sky beastfolk, even a great Oracle-grade existence would be unable to erase this avatar from the world out of thin air. This trait is even rarer than the Starbeast inheritance itself."
He was no longer the ignorant rookie who had first stepped into the starry sky.
He knew very well that since a great Oracle-grade could revive a living being from the Time River, they could also completely erase the existence of a living being from the Time River.
But with a Starbeast avatar, he would no longer need to fear a great Oracle-grade erasing the traces of his existence.
Although his style of doing things was unrestrained, deep in his bones, he valued his own safety greatly.
Perhaps because of the desperate struggles he had gone through in his previous lives, a trace of caution had always remained hidden deep in his heart.
He lowered his head and stared at the giant egg before him.
[Starbeast (Special)]
Grade: Divine-grade
Effect: A Starbeast egg that has yet to nurture a "spirit." Its nurturing can be accelerated through various heavenly treasures, or it can be nurtured through divine will and energy.
Special: One may brand it with Divine Blood and Divine Soul, forcefully giving birth to a "divine spirit." Once the divine spirit is born, it may possess the body of the Starbeast.
Explanation:

If this Starbeast egg is refined into an avatar, it will inherit all the racial traits of the Starbeast race—Fortune Points, bloodline power, inheritance, and so on.At the same time, this avatar will also bear the racial karma carried by the Starbeast race.This avatar and the main body will become two completely different individuals. Their thoughts, ways of doing things, and personalities will all be independent of each other, but the main body can exert an enormous influence over it.

Description: For a Starbeast egg to grow into a complete form, it must undergo nurturing, hatching, breaking out of the shell, infancy at the peak of legendary-grade, childhood at the peak of supreme-grade, youth at the peak of demi-sage rank, adulthood at the peak of Divine-grade after awakening part of its bloodline, and maturity at Oracle-grade after awakening its entire bloodline...

Each breakthrough between these stages requires an extremely long period of time. However, with the nourishment of heavenly treasures, or with treasures that alter the flow of time, its growth can be accelerated.
Daniel’s gaze lingered for a long time on the description that said "adulthood means peak Divine-grade, maturity means Oracle-grade."
The value of this beast egg was immeasurable!
He stored the giant egg away, then turned his gaze once again toward the distant depths of the star sea.
Visca Galaxy, the Myriad Races Alliance, Golden Holy Mountain, great Oracle-grade existences...
All the pieces had already been laid out. All that remained was for him to make the decisive move that would determine fate.
Daniel carefully read through all the information about the Starbeast egg and noticed one particular line.
The avatar would inherit the karma of its race!
He did not take this point to heart.
Compared to the endless benefits that obtaining a Starbeast avatar could bring, what did a little karma count for?
He immediately forced out his own Divine Blood, using his divine will as a guide, and slowly injected the crimson drop of blood into the Starbeast egg.
This process seemed to make ancient decrees echo beside his ears, as though they were coming from the far shore of distant space-time...
[Ding! You are infusing the Starbeast egg with Divine Blood.]
[Ding! You must split off a portion of your Divine Soul and brand it within to complete the low-grade ritual.]
Daniel listened to the system notification and attempted to split his Divine Soul.
Divine Soul was the highest form of the soul.
With his current Rank, he could already clearly sense those illusory yet truly existing soul veins. He could even control the flow speed of blood in every capillary within his body.
Splitting his Divine Soul was not particularly difficult for him.
"Hmph—"
He could not help but let out a muffled groan.
The pain of cutting the soul was a hundred times more excruciating than physical injury.
When a mortal body suffered heavy damage, the body would activate its protection mechanism, causing the person to fall unconscious to escape the pain.
But the tearing of the soul had no such protection.
That agony was like having one’s heart carved out and bones scraped clean. It made one wish for death.
[Ding! Soul brand complete.]
[You must continue branding it every day with Divine Blood and Divine Soul power until this Starbeast egg nurtures a complete "spirit."]
[Note: The birth of this "spirit" requires a total of 90 days.]
When Daniel heard this, he could not help but bare his teeth in pain.
This meant that he would have to endure this cruel agony day after day, for a full 90 days, until that "spirit" was born.
"Looks like I’ll have to feed this Starbeast egg some Sacred Materials."
If even the first step required such a long period of time, then if the later hatching and shell-breaking stages also followed the normal process, would he have to wait tens of thousands of years?
Daniel had never once thought of taking the ordinary path.
"I hold such a heaven-defying Millionfold Boost ability in my hands. How could I stupidly wait for so long?!"
Thinking of this, he activated the Ivahpin Scroll and stepped into the virtual world.
He immediately exchanged all of his remaining four million points for various ordinary Sacred Materials and fed them all to the Starbeast egg in one go.
[Ding! The Starbeast egg is accelerating its nurturing. The nurturing period for the "spirit" is expected to be shortened to 50 days!]
"As expected, it works, though it really burns through money."
Daniel shook his head. This cost was truly not low.

"But it doesn’t matter. As the territory I conquer grows wider and wider, and the resources I plunder become more and more abundant, Golden Holy Mountain’s points won’t amount to much in the future. Even emptying Golden Holy Mountain’s treasury might not be impossible!"
Aerial Realm.
[Ding! Aerial Realm has evolved into a middle living world.]
[Ding! The World Tree sapling has grown into a small World Tree.]
Daniel’s puppet avatar had long since watered the World Tree sapling with the Spring of Life.
At this moment, Aerial Realm had completely finished its transformation!
It had advanced from a small living world into a middle living world.
At the same time, army after army of players was assembling.
Aerial Realm’s starry sky teleportation passages were slowly opening.
Leading them were Daniel’s puppet avatar, Camille, Conrad, and a group of quasi-Divine-grade powerhouses.

Behind them were hundreds of elite players who had already reached the threshold of supreme-grade, tens of millions of legendary-grade players, and hundreds of millions of ordinary warriors clad in legendary-grade battle armor forged with magic-energy technology.
The players stared at the deep plane passages before them with surging excitement.
"The guild leader brought back so many rare treasures from the Endless Starsea. I want every single one of them."
"Who doesn’t? Those top-grade Divine Domain templates and the top-tier Sacred Materials for constructing Divine Domains... but all of them have to be exchanged with points."
"You get points by fighting wars. For the sake of becoming stronger, I wish we could go on campaigns every day."
"Do you think attacking several planes at the same time is a little too arrogant? Could something go wrong?"
"What’s there to be afraid of? Believe in the guild leader."
"Exactly. You can always trust the boss."
The other ends of the spatial passages connected to several small world planes.
They were territories under the command of primordial races such as the Godkin, shadowkin, and sirenfolk.
The curtain was about to rise on a plane invasion!
And this time, the ones launching the invasion were the players!
Daniel turned around and gazed at the vast, boundless army of players behind him. His eyes were filled with pride and a sense of accomplishment.
In his previous lives, humanity could only passively endure endless invasions like lambs waiting to be slaughtered.
But now, the players had risen up and become the initiators of invasions against other planes.
Although the youth who slays the dragon may one day become the dragon himself, it was still far better than being bullied forever!
If one did not want to be bullied, one had to become strong.
If one wanted to become strong, one had to fight for it.
If one did not fight, there was only a dead end!

chapters.title: Chapter 316 -316-Toward Glory Through Blood and Fire
paragraphs: Survival and reproduction would forever remain the foremost laws of any civilization.
Just like the world Camille had once called home—the Divine Wind Realm, a world that did not understand resistance. In the end, that entire civilization had been reduced to dust within the star sea.
Not a single soul had offered even the faintest gratitude to Camille, who had once fought with everything she had to protect that entire civilization.
"The living beings of the Divine Wind Realm were unworthy of Camille!"
"Those fools who thought themselves merciful deserved to become dust in the Time River, forgotten by all."
Several spatial passages slowly opened. Deep, dim radiance flowed through the void, like colossal beasts opening their maws.
Batch after batch of players held their heads high and marched forward in neat, orderly lines, stepping into the passages one after another.
On the other side of those passages lay unfamiliar otherworlds.
As the players moved forward, they spoke to one another in low voices.
"Sunborn, which plane were you assigned to?"
Hans asked.
"Rozeli World. The Guild Leader is personally leading the team."
Sunborn asked in return, "What about you?"
"Shrilair World. Lord Camille is leading us."
Hans smiled, then added, "I heard you took out quite a few loans from the bank and already used exchange points to purchase an excellent Divine Domain template?"
"Hahaha... even you know about that? But I’m still missing a lot of materials to construct the Divine Domain."
Sunborn laughed and said, "Still, it won’t take long. As long as there are missions to do, earning points is pretty fast. It shouldn’t be long before I gather all the materials."
"I’m so jealous. I want an excellent Divine Domain template too."
Hans looked at the spatial passage growing closer and closer, clenched his fists, and encouraged him in a low voice.
"Good luck."
"You too."
Sunborn’s figure gradually vanished into the light of the passage as well.
Whoosh—whoosh—whoosh—
Countless players surged into the otherworlds like a tide. Awaiting them would be campaign after campaign of conquest!
They would fall amid slaughter, rise again, and then continue seizing one plane after another.
With the resources plundered from otherworlds, they would become stronger, then move on to conquer even more powerful planes.
This cycle would repeat again and again, until one day, they grew into one of the most powerful races in this star sea.
Every race that stood at the summit had carved its way there step by step through killing!
Daniel was merely following the ancient and unchanging iron law of the Endless Starsea.
Pour in everything. Fight with everything. Seize everything!
The players, too, were walking this path.
If one did not fight for it, one would gain nothing.
The strong controlled everything. Everything belonging to the weak could be freely dominated and disposed of by the strong.
Rozeli World.
The otherworldly legions clashed head-on with the player army. Blades flashed, swords crossed, and magic skills flew wildly across the battlefield.
Boom!
Daniel summoned a shower of meteors, smashing a group of peak demi-sage-rank powerhouses from the otherworld into pieces. Immediately afterward, a system notification rang beside his ear.
Not far away, the players brandished blades and staves, sweeping over the enemy legions like a descending natural disaster.
Swish, swish. Whoosh, whoosh. Boom, boom...
Countless skills crisscrossed through the sky and across the ground. The earth split apart, and the heavens trembled.

In the eyes of the players, these otherworldly natives were nothing more than embodiments of experience points and gold coins. They were piles of walking skill books, equipment, Divine Domain templates, and rare materials!
Because of that, they fought with extraordinary ferocity, without the slightest restraint.
Even if they died, they would simply stand up again at the respawn point.
The native legions of the otherworld also resisted with all their might, their willpower astonishingly tenacious.
This was a war between two worlds. There was no room for reconciliation.
The war lasted for a very long time.
Most of the time, Daniel watched coldly from the sidelines. He had no intention of intervening lightly.
If the players wanted to grow, they could not remain forever under the shelter of his wings.
Flowers raised in a greenhouse would never survive for long.
He set his sights on looting the most valuable resources in this world, taking every rare treasure he could find into his possession.
At the same time, the conviction in his heart grew firmer and firmer. He felt increasingly certain that the path he had chosen was the correct one.
"Humanity cannot become puppets ruled and dominated by others. Humanity must be reborn in blood and fire!"
Visca Galaxy.
A fleet composed of eight Starships slowly sailed through the dark expanse of space.
The Endless Starsea clearly had convenient forms of transportation such as spatial passages and world portals, so why were there still people using such an ancient method of transportation as fleets?
Because the cost of using spatial passages was extremely high—far more expensive than portals.
Moreover, some planes were extremely closed off and conservative, and did not open spatial passages or portals at all.
Therefore, star fleets remained an indispensable means of transportation, still occupying an overwhelmingly dominant share in logistics and travel.
This was also the fundamental reason Astral Corsairs were so rampant in the Endless Starsea.
All eight of these Starships flew the flag of the Lionheart Realm, declaring their identity—a fleet of the Lionheart Realm, under the Myriad Races Alliance.
Under normal circumstances, no Astral Corsair lacking eyes would be willing to provoke a force of this level.
Besides, the fleet was not carrying any particularly valuable cargo, so neither the fleet commander nor the accompanying guards were especially powerful.
However, there were always exceptions to everything.
On the watchtower of the vanguard ship, the lookout suddenly noticed something unusual.
A powerhouse immediately reported the news upward.
"Captain, there are pirates blocking the way in the starfield ahead. They’re flying the Dawn Flag. Their signal says... they want us to submit obediently!"
The fleet captain sneered.
"Signal back. Tell those idiots to get lost immediately."
"Understood, Captain."
His subordinate immediately went down to deliver the order.
"This vast starry sky really does contain all sorts of trash."
The Starship captain watched his subordinate leave, shook his head indifferently, and wore a faint sneer at the corner of his mouth.
"Fools like this, who don’t know the height of the heavens or the depth of the earth, probably don’t even know how to write the word death—yet they dare try to snatch food from a dragon’s plate?"
On the Star Island.
Within the dark void, a floating rocky fortress radiated a sharp and menacing aura.
A Low Divine-grade pirate leader hurried up to Daniel, bowed, and reported. His voice carried an unconcealable trace of nervousness.
"My lord, we have discovered Starships flying the flag of the Lionheart Realm ahead."
He hesitated for a moment. His Adam’s apple bobbed, and he added,
"The Lionheart Realm is a major world in this galaxy. It belongs to the Myriad Races Alliance, and its strength is extremely formidable... Should we perhaps..."
Daniel did not allow him to finish.
He raised his eyes. His gaze was as cold as a blade, and his tone was indifferent yet unquestionable.
"Do you think my blade is not sharp enough, or do you think your own life is too long? Enough nonsense—rob them!"
His voice was not loud, yet it pressed down on the pirate leader until he nearly could not breathe.
"Yes, my lord!"
The Divine-grade pirate leader’s back was instantly soaked with cold sweat. He hurriedly bowed and withdrew.

He turned and leapt onto the command platform, personally steering that ferocious Star Island forward. Like an ancient beast awakening from its slumber, it moved to block the Lionheart Realm fleet head-on.
The alarm bells on the Starships abruptly tore through the void.
From the cabin of the leading Starship, a figure shot into the air.
It was a Divine-grade powerhouse clad in golden armor, his bearing majestic and dignified. He hovered in space, sacred light surging around him, his voice booming like thunder.
"What petty criminals dare obstruct the fleet of my Lionheart Realm? You hyenas of the starry sky—are you tired of living?"
Before his voice had even faded—
Boom!
In the starry sky, a colossal palm that blotted out the heavens suddenly appeared and came crashing down. Like a god crushing an ant, it smashed that Divine-grade powerhouse into powder on the spot.
"Kill!"
The Divine-grade pirate leader cast a fearful glance at that giant palm, then roared and charged forward with his blade raised.
"Kill! Kill! Kill!"
"Take them down!"
The densely packed pirates on the Star Island transformed into streaks of light and madly pounced toward the eight Starships.
Whoosh, whoosh, whoosh!
Boom, boom, boom!
The defensive weapons on the Starships continuously erupted with dazzling beams of energy, weaving into an airtight net of firepower.
No one knew how many Astral Corsairs were struck by that ferocious firepower and turned to ash on the spot.
Yet countless pirates still broke through the fire net, leaping onto the Starships and beginning boarding combat.
"You damned pirates! My Lionheart Realm will never let you go!"
A Divine-grade powerhouse saw that the fleet was about to fall into enemy hands and could not help but let out a furious roar.
Boom!
That giant palm descended once more, swatting that Divine-grade powerhouse apart together with his roar, as easily as crushing a fly.
Several Divine-grade powerhouses fled from the fleet in panic, attempting to escape.
However, beneath Daniel’s palm, no one could get away.
In the end, the Lionheart Realm’s Starship fleet fell entirely into Daniel’s hands!

chapters.title: Chapter 317 -317-The Endless Starsea Does Not Believe in the Tears of the Weak
paragraphs: Daniel’s thunderous actions were like a meteor crashing into the calm star sea, alarming countless powerhouses and factions.
This was especially true in the Myriad Races Starry Sky—almost every small world was suffering humanity’s storm-like invasions.
Ancient factions such as the Godkin, shadowkin, sirenfolk, and others were furious, yet none of them dared to speak out.
They had already offended Faustus once before. Now, they had received news that Gold-grade Mountain had already designated the entire Visca Galaxy as Faustus’s sphere of influence.
"In the name of the abyss, that fellow really is vindictive."
Several great lords of the Demon Realm sat around a long black table, shaking their heads and sighing helplessly.
"By the Creator, he is already the strongest quasi-sage in the current universe. Inside small worlds, there is simply nothing we can do to him, not to mention he has Gold-grade Mountain backing him."
Several clan chiefs of the demon race also let out long sighs during their secret meeting.
"Forget it. We’ll endure it. They are only some small worlds, after all."
"Alas—"
Within the halls of the God Realm, only a long and bitter sigh remained.
They had been held firmly in Faustus’s grasp, so tightly that they could not even summon the strength to struggle.

As for those powerhouses who did not belong to any of the three factions, but were also under Gold-grade Mountain’s command, and whose territories just happened to lie within the Visca Galaxy, they now found Daniel to be an immense headache as well.
"In the end, they are only small worlds. It is not worth going to war with him over them."
A sage leaned back in a chair inlaid with star diamonds and rubbed the space between his brows.
"If he dares to set his sights on medium life worlds, it will not be too late for us to act then."
"But what about the matter with the Astral Corsairs? Faustus has gone too far!"
Another powerhouse slammed the table and rose to his feet, fury burning in his eyes.
"We can report him to Gold-grade Mountain! He is disrupting the stability of the galaxy!"
"That’s right! Faustus has gone too far in bullying others!"
"File a complaint! File a complaint! Go to Gold-grade Mountain and accuse him!"
"You are all still too naive."
An elderly sage sneered, lifted his wine glass, and took a light sip.
"Faustus is currently a favorite in front of Lady Chanelle. Who would dare step forward to punish him?"
"A mere struggle over small worlds—such an insignificant little matter is not even worth those great figures above lifting their eyelids."
"We can endure the matter of the small worlds, but he organized Astral Corsairs and even plundered us along with everyone else. I cannot swallow this insult! We must file a complaint!"
"We are all forces under Gold-grade Mountain, yet he even attacks his own people. He is simply too arrogant!"
Waves of anger echoed through the hall like thunder before a storm.
Gold-grade Mountain headquarters.
Countless letters of complaint and reports against Faustus piled up like mountains. Wave after wave of envoys came to deliver formal accusations.
However—
All the letters were forcefully suppressed, and every envoy was denied entry. The guards merely coldly threw down a single sentence.
"We are not receiving visitors."
Gold-grade Mountain’s attitude could not have been more obvious—they were blatantly shielding Faustus!
In this star sea, rules had never been decided by mouths.
An Oracle-grade powerhouse of Gold-grade Mountain had once casually said the following words.
"Fighting over territory is perfectly normal. If you cannot win, then obediently give it up—that is a truth even worms in the abyss understand."

"Since when has the Endless Starsea become a place where people can sit down and reason with one another? The tears of the weak have never been able to extinguish the flames of war lit by the strong."
He paused. A trace of coldness flashed through his eyes as he continued.
"Faustus is seizing territory. We will not interfere. That is his ability, and it is also your incompetence."
"But if you dare dispatch an Oracle-grade powerhouse, or a peak Divine-grade powerhouse, to deal with him—listen carefully. In that case, we will have no choice but to interfere!"
"Rules are rules. Whoever flips the table first should not blame us for tearing down the entire house."
"Do you know how to write the word fairness?"
He slowly clenched his fist. His knuckles cracked sharply, and a mocking smile rose at the corner of his lips.
"Fist—this word is pronounced as ’fairness.’ Do you understand?"
After saying this, he turned and left, leaving behind a silent room and those envoys who dared to be angry but did not dare to speak.
Earth.
System notifications exploded beside Daniel’s ears like a tsunami.
[Ding! You have obtained Meteorite Gold × 100 million units!]
[Ding! You sold Meteorite Gold × 100 million units to Doom Guild for 1 copper coin, triggering Millionfold Boost! Please choose quality boost/quantity boost!]
"Quantity boost!"
[Congratulations! You have obtained 1 gold coin! You have obtained Meteorite Gold × 10 billion units!]
[Ding! You have obtained Realm Crystal × 100 million units!]
[Ding! You sold Realm Crystal × 100 million units to Doom Guild for 1 copper coin, triggering Millionfold Boost!... You have obtained Realm Crystal × 10 billion units!]
[Ding! You have obtained Heart of Kalitz × 100 million!]
[... You have obtained Heart of Kalitz × 10 billion!]
The notification sounds rang out densely, one after another.
[Ding! You have absorbed the power of World Origin!]
[Ding! You have obtained Misty Divine Water, a Primordial Sacred Material × 1!]
[Ding! Millionfold Boost triggered. You have obtained Misty Divine Water × 1,000,000 wisps!]
[Ding! You have mastered the power of faith!]
[... Ding! Millionfold Boost triggered! You have obtained Holy Spirit’s Breath, Divine-grade × 1 wisp!]
[... You have obtained Holy Spirit’s Breath × 1,000,000 wisps!]
[Ding! You have absorbed...]
Daniel exchanged all these overwhelming resources into Gold-grade Mountain points.
[Ding! You have successfully exchanged them for 1.02 billion Gold-grade Mountain points.]
Listening to the notifications beside his ears, Daniel was in an extraordinarily wonderful mood.
Over the past half year, every once in a while, he would exchange the resources he had plundered in batches for points.
He had not spared a single resource that could be boosted into Divine-grade.
After boosting them, he would exchange them again, earning hundreds of millions of points each time.
All things considered, these resources had brought him over ten billion Gold-grade Mountain points!
Because of Millionfold Boost, he could profit from both ends.

First, he boosted resources by ten thousand times and exchanged them for points. Then, he used those points to exchange for treasures, before allowing the players to redeem those treasures with guild points at reasonable prices.

Although Daniel was harvesting hundreds of billions of players, he was also giving those players countless opportunities that ordinary natives could never obtain no matter how hard they struggled throughout their lives.
Such opportunities were priceless!
But even after this kind of millionfold-boosted trading had continued for half a year, he had only accumulated several tens of billions of points.
Just exchanging for Divine-grade secret treasures alone had cost nearly twenty billion.
"The Starbeast egg has already reached the point where it is about to hatch under the nourishment of a large number of Holy Relics."
A smile appeared on Daniel’s face.
"If it had been nurtured by conventional means, it would probably have taken tens of thousands of years. It is precisely because of these resources that its progress has advanced so quickly."
That Starbeast egg had already nurtured a "spirit."
His clone plan was progressing extremely smoothly.
"But... it is still not enough!"
He had exchanged for a Divine-grade secret treasure used for advancement—the Chrono Temple!
It was an incomparably magnificent building, and its core function was to adjust the flow of time.
The Chrono Temple’s time flow could reach ten thousand times that of the outside world!
What kind of concept was that?
It was equivalent to staying inside the temple for one day while ten thousand years passed in the outside world.
Conversely, it could also be set so that ten thousand years passed inside the temple while only one day passed in the outside world.

You have obtained 1 gold coin!
You have obtained Meteorite Gold × 10 billion units!]
[Ding!
You have obtained Realm Crystal × 100 million units!]
[Ding!
You sold Realm Crystal × 100 million units to Doom Guild for 1 copper coin, triggering Millionfold Boost!...
You have obtained Realm Crystal × 10 billion units!]
[Ding!
You have obtained Heart of Kalitz × 100 million!]
You have obtained Heart of Kalitz × 10 billion!]
The notification sounds rang out densely, one after another.
[Ding!
You have absorbed the power of World Origin!]
[Ding!
You have obtained Misty Divine Water, a Primordial Sacred Material × 1!]
[Ding!
Millionfold Boost triggered.
You have obtained Misty Divine Water × 1,000,000 wisps!]
[Ding!
You have mastered the power of faith!]
Ding!
Millionfold Boost triggered!
You have obtained Holy Spirit’s Breath, Divine-grade × 1 wisp!]
You have obtained Holy Spirit’s Breath × 1,000,000 wisps!]
[Ding!
You have absorbed...]
Daniel exchanged all these overwhelming resources into Gold-grade Mountain points.
[Ding!
You have successfully exchanged them for 1.02 billion Gold-grade Mountain points.]
Listening to the notifications beside his ears, Daniel was in an extraordinarily wonderful mood.
Over the past half year, every once in a while, he would exchange the resources he had plundered in batches for points.
He had not spared a single resource that could be boosted into Divine-grade.
After boosting them, he would exchange them again, earning hundreds of millions of points each time.
All things considered, these resources had brought him over ten billion Gold-grade Mountain points!
Because of Millionfold Boost, he could profit from both ends.
First, he boosted resources by ten thousand times and exchanged them for points.
Then, he used those points to exchange for treasures, before allowing the players to redeem those treasures with guild points at reasonable prices.

Although Daniel was harvesting hundreds of billions of players, he was also giving those players countless opportunities that ordinary natives could never obtain no matter how hard they struggled throughout their lives.
Such opportunities were priceless!
But even after this kind of millionfold-boosted trading had continued for half a year, he had only accumulated several tens of billions of points.
Just exchanging for Divine-grade secret treasures alone had cost nearly twenty billion.
"The Starbeast egg has already reached the point where it is about to hatch under the nourishment of a large number of Holy Relics."
A smile appeared on Daniel’s face.
"If it had been nurtured by conventional means, it would probably have taken tens of thousands of years.
It is precisely because of these resources that its progress has advanced so quickly."
That Starbeast egg had already nurtured a "spirit."
His clone plan was progressing extremely smoothly.
"But... it is still not enough!"
He had exchanged for a Divine-grade secret treasure used for advancement—the Chrono Temple!
It was an incomparably magnificent building, and its core function was to adjust the flow of time.
The Chrono Temple’s time flow could reach ten thousand times that of the outside world!
What kind of concept was that?
It was equivalent to staying inside the temple for one day while ten thousand years passed in the outside world.
Conversely, it could also be set so that ten thousand years passed inside the temple while only one day passed in the outside world.

chapters.title: Chapter 318 -318-Chrono Temple, Imperial Bow Ark
paragraphs: [Chrono Temple (Sacred Artisan Law Grade)]
Type: Auxiliary
Level: Sacred Artisan Law Grade
Law: Spacetime Law
Effect: Can adjust the flow of time within spacetime, either forward or in reverse.
Special: The upper limit of the spacetime flow rate is ten thousand times.
Required Points: 5 billion points

Description: A Divine-grade secret treasure of the Spacetime Law category, meticulously crafted by a Great Oracle-grade existence. It is used to assist with advancement and is incomparably rare and precious!

The Spacetime Law was a supreme-grade law of the universe. It was even more precious than ordinary Primordial Grade Holy Relics. Therefore, the number of points required to exchange for it was extremely high.
Daniel placed the Starbeast egg into the Chrono Temple.
In just a few days, that Starbeast clone body would be born.
The Chrono Temple was only one of his gains during this period.
He had also spent one billion points to purchase Divine-grade resources and completely undo the seal on the Voidbound Grail.
Now, this Holy Grail had become one of the most useful Divine-grade secret treasures in his possession.
"If not for this half year of frenzied expansion..."
Daniel pondered, his fingertips lightly tapping against the back of his chair.
"How long would it have taken me to accumulate this many resources? Without resources, how could I have used Millionfold Boost to pry open such a massive amount of Gold-grade Mountain points?"
"Only with points do I have the chance to become stronger. Divine-grade secret treasures, Sacred Arts, Divine Domain templates—these are all steps on the ladder to greater strength."
Over the past half year, he had already occupied fifteen galaxies, including the Myriad Races Starry Sky, and eighty-nine small worlds. The resources he had obtained were beyond counting.
And the players’ efforts had also been rewarded!

By helping Daniel expand his sphere of influence, they had earned enormous amounts of guild points. Using those guild points, they exchanged for Divine Domain templates brought back by Daniel from Gold-grade Mountain, Sacred Materials used to construct Divine Domains, as well as many Sacred Arts and other resources that could make them stronger.
Daniel gazed through the porthole at the boundless star sea outside. A satisfied curve rose at the corner of his lips.
"Several tens of thousands of players have already broken through to supreme-grade."
He spoke softly, his voice carrying a hint of pride, like a gardener inspecting the garden he had carefully watered at dawn.
"Moreover, their strength is considered first-rate even among supreme-grade existences. They are not empty shells forcefully piled up with resources, but true warriors tempered by blood and fire."
He nodded slightly.
"It is precisely because there is an endless stream of resources that they can break through so rapidly."
His gaze grew deep, as though he were staring into an even more distant future.
"The stronger they become, the richer the benefits I will obtain in the future. This is a trade where I cannot possibly lose."
"Now, everything has already entered the track I envisioned. The star sea is the chessboard, all living beings are the chess pieces, and I must sit in the position of the chess player!"
He blinked, and stars seemed to flow within his eyes.
"It is time to rendezvous with Dustin."
He stood up, his robes silently stirring in the void.
"The journey to the Astral Realm will definitely be a grand hunt. Perhaps I can directly break through to Divine-grade there and step into the level of peak Divine-grade in one stroke."
He took out a Divine-grade secret treasure from his personal space.
It was a starry-sky flight-type Divine-grade secret treasure he had exchanged for in Ivahpin World at the cost of eight billion points—the Imperial Bow Ark!
The ship’s hull was long and slender, its entire body flowing with starlight, as though it were a solidified galaxy.
At this moment, the engines of the sacred ship rumbled softly in the void, like the roar of an ancient beast awakening from its slumber!
[Imperial Bow Ark (Primordial Law Grade)]
Type: Auxiliary Flying Vehicle
Level: Primordial Law Grade—a supreme-grade tier among Divine-grade secret treasures, forged from Origin matter born at the beginning of the universe and containing complete Law power.
Core Law: Spacetime Law
Functions:
Voidbreaker: Can forcibly tear through and break past all spatial blockades and suppression beneath Great Oracle-grade, like a sharp blade cutting open a curtain.

Spatial Shield: Once activated, layer upon layer of spatial defensive shields will automatically form around the hull, capable of withstanding the vast majority of attacks beneath Great Oracle-grade. Its defense is as solid as an impregnable fortress.
Cruising: Its flight speed is comparable to that of an Oracle-grade existence, allowing it to cross galaxies in an instant.

Special: Requires the consumption of vast amounts of resources when used. The longer it operates and the faster it moves, the more terrifying the consumption becomes, like a bottomless abyssal maw that can never be filled.
Required Points: 8 billion points

Description: This ship is an exceptional treasure among Spacetime Law-type Divine-grade secret treasures. It was meticulously crafted by a Great Oracle-grade existence who poured his heart and soul into it, specially designed for long-distance voyages and combat across the star sea. If all of its functions are fully activated, it will transform into a bottomless black hole that devours precious materials—those without a deep enough fortune would not even be qualified to feed it scraps!
Daniel had always placed great importance on both the experience of travel and his own safety.
When it came to flight-type Divine-grade vehicles, he either would not buy one at all, or he would buy the very best.
The Imperial Bow Ark was one of the rarest treasures among treasures in Gold-grade Mountain’s treasury.
Even those high-ranking Oracle-grade existences would not be able to resist taking a few extra glances at it, secretly feeling envious in their hearts.
Of course, its consumption was also terrifying enough to make one’s tongue click in disbelief.
The description had stated it clearly: when all of its functions were fully activated, this ship was a greedy beast that could never be fed!
Forget ordinary Divine-grade powerhouses—even among those lofty Divine Radiants and Divine Sovereigns, very few had the wealth to casually operate it.
But Daniel did.

His subordinates now controlled several dozen small worlds. Although the absolute quality of those resources could not be considered the very pinnacle of the star sea, after being enhanced by Millionfold Boost, their quality was already no weaker than the top-tier output of those major worlds.

The strength of the resources in his hands lay in their ocean-like quantity. With the enhancement system backing him up, he had accumulated a batch of resources astonishing enough to leave anyone dumbfounded.
Not only that, he had also exchanged for several Divine-grade secret treasures for Camille to use in self-defense.
At this moment, he still had over one billion Gold-grade Mountain points on him. That was enough for the Imperial Bow Ark to stretch its limbs and squander resources freely for a while.

He had already calculated everything clearly in his heart: he would leave behind a puppet clone to watch over the Starbeast clone body that was currently being nurtured, while also suppressing those restless schemers harboring evil intentions.
As for himself, he would bring Camille and head straight for Budelica Starfield.
"My lord."
Camille stood before the Imperial Bow Ark, whose entire body flowed with starlight. His eyes were filled with wonder and shock.
Hot blood surged in his chest, and even his voice trembled slightly.
"Are we... going to the Astral Realm?"
Daniel smiled faintly. That smile carried both calm confidence and a hidden sharpness.
"That’s right."
"That’s wonderful!"
Camille almost jumped up, flames of desire burning in his eyes.
He had heard Daniel describe the many wonders of the Astral Realm in detail.
It was one of the sacred lands that all quasi-sages dreamed of, because buried there were the most top-tier and rarest opportunities in the entire Endless Starsea.
"Every time the Astral Realm opens, it is the best chance for large numbers of top-tier demi-sage-rank existences to break through."
Camille clenched his fists. He had been stuck at the quasi-sage rank for who knew how many years, and his heart had long been desperately starving for advancement.
He could not wait to search for an opportunity that belonged to him and break through to Divine-grade in one stroke.
Sage—just thinking about it filled him with excitement.
"We’re setting off."
Daniel stepped onto the boarding stairs of the Imperial Bow Ark. He looked back at the world behind him and laughed softly.
"Let’s go see with our own eyes that legendary Astral Realm—a place that even Oracle-grade existences cannot help but look upon with serious attention."

chapters.title: Chapter 319 -319-Part-Time Robbery
paragraphs: Whoosh!
The Imperial Bow Ark instantly sailed out of the plane and appeared in the vast, boundless starry sky.
Buzz!
The space around the ship suddenly distorted, and layers of ripples spread out in every direction.
In the brief gap between those rippling waves, the Imperial Bow Ark slipped into them like a nimble fish. In the blink of an eye, it vanished without a trace.
Somewhere deep within the starry sky, space trembled once more.
The Imperial Bow Ark quietly emerged from the void. After a brief pause, it repeated that miraculous journey of spatial leaping once again.
Daniel leaned back in the command seat, experiencing the Imperial Bow Ark’s astonishing method of movement. Countless thoughts rose in his heart.

"The way this ship travels is rather like the ’space warp’ from Earth’s ancient theories—jumping directly from one point to another without crossing any physical distance in between. It is countless times faster than simple flight."
He recalled that Earth had once proposed a technological concept known as a "warp drive," and it was strikingly similar to the scene before his eyes.
It was just that Earth’s path of development had long since been completely diverted by the fusion of game and reality, setting foot on an entirely different road.
"Still—"
The corners of his lips rose slightly, and the stars flashing past outside the porthole were reflected in his eyes.
"All roads lead to Rome."
"Whether technology or magic, in the end, they all point toward the deepest truth within this boundless star sea!"
"My lord, this Imperial Bow Ark truly is a miracle of the star sea."
Camille gazed at the stars sweeping rapidly past outside the porthole and could not help murmuring in awe. His voice was filled with reverence.
"Indeed."
Daniel nodded. A faint smile hung at the corner of his mouth.
"A Divine-grade secret treasure of this level is something even those lofty Oracle-grade existences would covet if they saw it!"

"Our destination is Budelica Starfield. Starting from Canaan Starfield, who knows how many galaxies and star rivers lie between us? The journey is so distant that it would be enough to make one despair."
"If not for this Imperial Bow Ark, honestly traveling there would probably take several hundred years."
Budelica Starfield and Canaan Starfield did not border each other. Several starfields lay between them.
The territory of a single galaxy alone was enough to make an ordinary Divine-grade powerhouse spend years traveling through it.
Above galaxies were star rivers, and above star rivers were starfields.
One could imagine just how long the journey from Canaan Starfield to Budelica Starfield truly was.
This was also why flight-type Divine-grade vehicles were even more precious than other types of Divine-grade secret treasures.
The more exceptional the flying vehicle, the rarer and harder to obtain it was.
And the Imperial Bow Ark had cost Daniel a full eight billion points to exchange for!
"However, some regions in the starry sky are sealed off. There are also forbidden lands and astral ruins that even Oracle-grade existences are unwilling to set foot in."
Daniel had read many ancient texts in Ivahpin World, so he was already extremely familiar with these common facts.
"Our route can only follow the established Star Chart. If we recklessly charge around and deviate from the course..."
He smiled, and a trace of coldness flashed through his eyes.

"We might accidentally barge into the territory of some major faction, or into the private backyard of an Oracle-grade existence, or even plunge headfirst into one of those forbidden regions of the starry sky that even Great Oracle-grade existences dare not enter deeply."
"In short, the risk is enormous! After all, danger is hidden everywhere in this star sea. Every step must be taken carefully. There is no such thing as being too cautious."
Camille nodded deeply in agreement, his hand subconsciously resting on the hilt of his sword.
"We have already left the Visca Galaxy."
Daniel glanced at the Star Chart and spoke calmly.
"Now, we have entered the Firefly Starfield."
Firefly Starfield.
Shimmering Galaxy.
Dozens of Starships shuttled back and forth along the galaxy’s route. Like busy worker ants, they were setting up an enormous formation.
Soon, the final formation mark lit up, and the entire formation was complete.
"Vice Speaker, the Space-Sealing Grand Formation has been fully arranged."
A powerhouse from the Council of the Gods quickly walked up to a high-grade sage and reported respectfully.
"From this moment onward, any starry sky traveler who passes through our galaxy will find it impossible to escape, even if they grow wings."
The Vice Speaker was named Sean. He nodded faintly, his gaze cold and indifferent.
This was far from the first time the Council of the Gods had engaged in the business of Astral Corsairs.
It was just that in the past, they had always disguised themselves as roaming pirates and gone to other starfields to plunder.
This time, however, they had paid a considerable price to exchange for this space-sealing formation from a certain major faction. Now they could sit comfortably and wait for good news.
After all, roaming around to plunder carried great risks!
You never knew whether the next ship contained a fat sheep or the incarnation of a dragon.
But waiting for prey on one’s own territory was much safer. The risk was lower, yet the gains were still considerable.
"Wait for the prey to arrive."
Sean’s tone was cold.

The powerhouses of the Council of the Gods silently hid within the void. Like a pack of wolves waiting in the dark for prey to walk into their trap, they patiently waited for unsuspecting travelers to enter the snare they had carefully laid.
In the Endless Starsea, robbery was not the specialty of pirates alone.
When the major factions had nothing better to do, they would occasionally take it up as a side job as well.
On ordinary days, everyone was a law-abiding citizen of the starry sky.
But once the time came to hunt, they would suddenly transform into bandits who burned, killed, and plundered!
The Council of the Gods was now at a critical stage of development. To advance from a small faction into a medium-sized one, they needed a massive amount of resources!
Where would those resources come from?
They could only rob others!
Was the Endless Starsea not simply a place where everyone plundered one another?
The weak were prey to the strong. It was only natural!
Shimmering Galaxy.
A wave of spatial fluctuation rippled through the void, and a Starship emerged from the star sea through a spatial leap.
That Starship was completely different from ordinary Starships. It was larger, more luxurious, and its appearance was incomparably elegant and streamlined!
On the outer shell of the vessel was painted a majestic Gold Holy Mountain emblem, but it flew no flag.
This showed that it was not a merchant ship, but a private travel vessel!
A travel vessel connected to Gold Holy Mountain.
However, while it was true that Gold Holy Mountain dominated Canaan Starfield, its authority did not extend all the way to Firefly Starfield.
"We have now arrived at Shimmering Galaxy in Firefly Starfield."
Daniel looked at the Star Chart, his finger slowly tracing along the route.
"After passing through another three starfields, twenty-five star rivers, and more than two hundred galaxies, we will reach Budelica Starfield."
Before his voice had even faded—
The Imperial Bow Ark suddenly trembled, as if it had collided with an invisible wall!
The entire ship came to an abrupt halt, unable to move.
"Hmm?"
Daniel raised an eyebrow, and a cold gleam flashed through his eyes.
"What is this? Astral Corsairs?"
Camille’s eyes snapped open. Killing intent surged within them like an awakened lion.
"A space-sealing magic array..."
Daniel murmured. The corners of his mouth sank slightly.
"Prepare for battle."
"Yes, my lord."
Camille immediately rose to his feet. His longsword left its sheath, its cold light reflecting across his face.
Daniel closed his eyes and brought up the threads of causality.
Sure enough, among the densely packed threads of causality before him, interwoven like a net, several hundred were glowing with a glaring brightness!
He slowly opened them one by one, and a cold smile gradually appeared on his face.
That smile was as frigid as a blade of ice in the depths of winter!

A powerhouse from the Council of the Gods quickly walked up to a high-grade sage and reported respectfully.
"From this moment onward, any starry sky traveler who passes through our galaxy will find it impossible to escape, even if they grow wings."
The Vice Speaker was named Sean.
He nodded faintly, his gaze cold and indifferent.
This was far from the first time the Council of the Gods had engaged in the business of Astral Corsairs.
It was just that in the past, they had always disguised themselves as roaming pirates and gone to other starfields to plunder.
This time, however, they had paid a considerable price to exchange for this space-sealing formation from a certain major faction.
Now they could sit comfortably and wait for good news.
After all, roaming around to plunder carried great risks!
You never knew whether the next ship contained a fat sheep or the incarnation of a dragon.
But waiting for prey on one’s own territory was much safer.
The risk was lower, yet the gains were still considerable.
"Wait for the prey to arrive."
Sean’s tone was cold.
The powerhouses of the Council of the Gods silently hid within the void.
Like a pack of wolves waiting in the dark for prey to walk into their trap, they patiently waited for unsuspecting travelers to enter the snare they had carefully laid.
In the Endless Starsea, robbery was not the specialty of pirates alone.
When the major factions had nothing better to do, they would occasionally take it up as a side job as well.
On ordinary days, everyone was a law-abiding citizen of the starry sky.
But once the time came to hunt, they would suddenly transform into bandits who burned, killed, and plundered!
The Council of the Gods was now at a critical stage of development.
To advance from a small faction into a medium-sized one, they needed a massive amount of resources!
Where would those resources come from?
They could only rob others!
Was the Endless Starsea not simply a place where everyone plundered one another?
The weak were prey to the strong.
It was only natural!
Shimmering Galaxy.
A wave of spatial fluctuation rippled through the void, and a Starship emerged from the star sea through a spatial leap.
That Starship was completely different from ordinary Starships.
It was larger, more luxurious, and its appearance was incomparably elegant and streamlined!
On the outer shell of the vessel was painted a majestic Gold Holy Mountain emblem, but it flew no flag.
This showed that it was not a merchant ship, but a private travel vessel!
A travel vessel connected to Gold Holy Mountain.
However, while it was true that Gold Holy Mountain dominated Canaan Starfield, its authority did not extend all the way to Firefly Starfield.
"We have now arrived at Shimmering Galaxy in Firefly Starfield."
Daniel looked at the Star Chart, his finger slowly tracing along the route.
"After passing through another three starfields, twenty-five star rivers, and more than two hundred galaxies, we will reach Budelica Starfield."
Before his voice had even faded—
The Imperial Bow Ark suddenly trembled, as if it had collided with an invisible wall!
The entire ship came to an abrupt halt, unable to move.
"Hmm?"
Daniel raised an eyebrow, and a cold gleam flashed through his eyes.
"What is this?
Astral Corsairs?"
Camille’s eyes snapped open.
Killing intent surged within them like an awakened lion.
"A space-sealing magic array..."
Daniel murmured.
The corners of his mouth sank slightly.
"Prepare for battle."
"Yes, my lord."
Camille immediately rose to his feet.
His longsword left its sheath, its cold light reflecting across his face.
Daniel closed his eyes and brought up the threads of causality.
Sure enough, among the densely packed threads of causality before him, interwoven like a net, several hundred were glowing with a glaring brightness!
He slowly opened them one by one, and a cold smile gradually appeared on his face.
That smile was as frigid as a blade of ice in the depths of winter!

chapters.title: Chapter 320 -320-The Prey Appears, Double Joy Descends!
paragraphs: "The rabbit has appeared!"
The lookout of the Council of the Gods shouted excitedly.
"It came from Canaan Starfield—a Starship of Gold Holy Mountain."
A powerhouse quickly walked up to Sean and reported in a low voice.
"Vice Speaker, we have discovered a Starship ahead. It is not flying any flag, but the hull bears the emblem of Gold Holy Mountain."
"We cannot determine what level that Starship is. Our preliminary estimate is that it is at least a Divine-grade vehicle above Sacred Artisan Grade."
Sean had already seen the Imperial Bow Ark.
It hovered quietly in the void, its entire body flowing with faint starlight, like an elegant yet dangerous starry-sky beast.
His eyes flickered, and his voice was hoarse and low.
"Gold Holy Mountain may cover the sky with one hand in Canaan Starfield, but this is Firefly Starfield. We are not afraid of it here."
"Vice Speaker..."
The powerhouse hesitated for a moment, then lowered his voice.
"That Starship is clearly no ordinary vessel. What if there is an Oracle-grade existence inside, or a large group of peak Divine-grade powerhouses? How should we handle that?"
In the Endless Starsea, anyone capable of owning such a magnificent Starship could not possibly be an ordinary figure.
After all, if one did not possess sufficient strength yet still dared to flaunt wealth so openly, how was that any different from courting death?
"It’s fine."
The corners of Sean’s mouth rose slightly, revealing a cold smile.

"Our God-Revealing Mirror has not reacted at all. That means the other party is merely below peak Divine-grade. Are the hundreds of Divine-grade powerhouses of our Council of the Gods supposed to fear one little Starship?"
The God-Revealing Mirror was also a type of Divine-grade secret treasure, and it had an extremely wide range of uses.

It could precisely detect the strength of powerhouses below peak Divine-grade. That was because powerhouses at that level were still unable to fully restrain their divine energy. Divine energy would always leak from their bodies from time to time, and the God-Revealing Mirror could easily capture those energy fluctuations.
As for Oracle-grade existences... this kind of basic space-sealing formation could not trap beings of that level at all.
If there truly were an Oracle-grade existence on that ship, they would have already broken out of the formation long ago. They would never remain stalled like this Starship before them.
The cold smile on Sean’s face deepened.
"The strongest person on that Starship is at most a high-grade sage. Our luck is quite good today."
Before his voice had even faded, the lookout cried out again in surprise.
"Hm? There’s another one!"
At the same time, spatial fluctuations rippled through the void once more.
Another Starship emerged from a spatial leap. It was likewise firmly trapped by the Council of the Gods’ space-sealing magic array and could not move at all.
Sean’s eyes immediately lit up!
Could today be a day blessed by fate?
Why were prey arriving like a tide, wave after wave, throwing themselves right into his hands?
Just a few minutes after Daniel’s Imperial Bow Ark had been seized by the ankles like by an invisible giant hand, another Starship also fell into the Council of the Gods’ space-sealing formation.

The specifications of that Starship were far inferior to Daniel’s vessel. After all, the Imperial Bow Ark was a rare treasure that even Oracle-grade existences would covet—a legendary ship that sailed through the depths of the star sea.
The ship before them was merely a little more luxurious than an ordinary merchant vessel.
At its prow hung a flag, and embroidered upon the flag was the emblem of a major world somewhere in Firefly Starfield, fluttering faintly in the void.
It looked like a merchant cargo ship.
"Vice Speaker..."
Sean raised an eyebrow, and an excited smile appeared on his lips.
He narrowed his eyes and looked at the two trapped ships.
Then he turned toward the powerhouse beside him and said in an icy tone,
"Tell all travelers aboard those two Starships to come down."
His subordinate immediately accepted the order. Signal flags flashed in the dark void like silent warnings.
Daniel had already withdrawn the threads of causality.
That invisible thread of fate had displayed the entire chain of cause and effect before his eyes. He had already made his decision.
The unexpected appearance of that merchant Starship had also been included within his causal foresight, without the slightest deviation.
"My lord, they have sent a signal flag ordering us to abandon ship and come down."
During this period, Camille had commanded the Astral Corsairs in battle, so he was already extremely familiar with the signal flags used by the major factions of the Endless Starsea.
He glanced at the flashing light signals across from them and explained calmly.
"Wait for now."
The corners of Daniel’s mouth rose slightly, revealing a meaningful smile.
There was no panic in that smile, no anger, only the calm composure of a hunter watching his prey step into a trap.
Camille nodded thoughtfully, then turned his gaze toward the trapped merchant Starship not far away.
That ship had also received the signal flag from the Council of the Gods, but it showed no intention of surrendering.
Whoosh!
A streak of light shot out from that Starship and transformed into a High Divine-grade powerhouse in the void.
Holy light coiled around the man’s body as he hovered within the space-sealing formation and called out across the distance.
"May I ask whether the esteemed individuals opposite us are powerhouses of the Council of the Gods?"
"I am Zoran of Windrest World. I was merely passing through this place on my way to conduct business. Might you be willing to show some flexibility and allow us to leave safely?"
"If Your Excellency is willing to be magnanimous, Windrest World will surely remember this favor."
The camp of the Council of the Gods remained silent for a moment, as though mocking such a naive request.
Then the signal flags lit up once again, crimson points of light flickering in the darkness.
"In this star sea, only blades and swords have ever had the right to speak. If we showed flexibility to everyone, what would be the point of this?"
"Surrender immediately and give up resisting. Otherwise, we will make sure you die without even bone fragments left behind!"
Zoran’s expression immediately darkened.
His Starship had already been firmly suppressed by the space-sealing formation. The hull trembled faintly, unable to perform a spatial leap or break through the boundary and leave!
Powerhouses below Oracle-grade were all unable to tear apart this locked-down void.
But what merchant would carry an army around with them?
There were only a few dozen Divine-grade guards aboard Zoran’s Starship. How could they possibly be a match for the several hundred sages of the Council of the Gods opposite them?
"I’m afraid I’m doomed today!"
Zoran’s heart sank.
At that moment, a thought crawled up his spine like a cold snake.
He could not help glancing toward the Imperial Bow Ark hovering quietly nearby. The owner of that ship still had not shown themselves, nor had they sent out any distress signal!
If that ship also had several dozen powerhouses aboard, perhaps they would still have a chance to fight.
But that hope was as faint as a speck of dust in the depths of the star sea.
Just as Zoran was hesitating, Sean in the distance had already lost the last of his patience.
He coldly spat out a single word, filled with unquestionable cruelty.
"Kill."
Whoosh! Whoosh! Whoosh!
Hundreds of Divine-grade powerhouses transformed into streaks of light. Like torrential rain, and like falling stellar bodies, they pounced toward Zoran from every direction.
As for Daniel’s side, they had already determined that the powerhouses on that ship had been scared out of their wits.
"Face the enemy!"
Zoran gritted his teeth and ordered the powerhouses under his command to prepare for battle.
However, only a few Divine-grade powerhouses flew out from behind him. The rest either shrank back in fear or had no fighting spirit at all.
Surrendering would not necessarily cost them their lives. At worst, they would be captured and made prisoners.
But if they resisted, death was certain.
These guards had families and foundations waiting for them. They did not dare directly oppose the Council of the Gods at all.
Preserving one’s life came first. That was an instinct carved into the bones of every living being!

chapters.title: Chapter 321 -321-The Prey and the Hunter
paragraphs: "My lord..."
Camille looked at the one-sided slaughter unfolding in the void. The powerhouses of the Council of the Gods were surging toward Zoran’s side like a tide.
"No rush."
Daniel smiled. His tone was as calm as if he were discussing the weather.
He leaned back in the command seat, his gaze as still as water.
"I have a Divine-grade secret treasure that can break this space-sealing formation, but there is no need to hurry. Our luck is quite good. We encountered someone interesting the moment we set out."
Hearing this, Camille could not help but smile knowingly.
He had followed Daniel for so long that he had long since understood his way of doing things.
He said softly, "I understand what you mean, my lord."
"The Council of the Gods thinks they have us firmly in their grasp, but what they don’t know is that we can leave, yet choose not to. We’re just playing along with them."
"Once both sides have fought each other to exhaustion, we can swallow them all in one move!"
He remembered something Faustus often said: a truly skilled hunter often appears in the guise of prey.
Daniel did not answer. The curve at the corner of his mouth merely deepened.
In the void, the slaughter continued. Holy light and blood intertwined into a cruel painting of the star sea.
And he quietly waited for the moment of harvest.

The several hundred Divine-grade powerhouses of the Council of the Gods effortlessly killed Zoran and the few Divine-grade powerhouses beside him on the spot. Afterward, they casually took control of the merchant Starship belonging to Windrest World.

Once they were done, they were like a pack of bloodthirsty wolves. They quickly turned around and surrounded the Imperial Bow Ark, which still hovered silently in the void—layer upon layer, sealing it off so tightly that not even water could pass through.
Whoosh!
The void suddenly trembled, and Daniel’s figure appeared without warning. His robes fluttered, and his expression was indifferent.
The many Divine-grade powerhouses of the Council of the Gods froze at the same time. Then they burst into mocking laughter.
"A quasi-sage?"
Sean was first stunned, then a trace of ridicule appeared at the corner of his mouth.
"No wonder he hid inside the ship and didn’t dare move. So he’s merely a demi-sage rank..."
His voice suddenly stopped. A hint of suspicion flashed through his eyes.
He stared deeply at Daniel, and his heart abruptly shook. That face, that figure, gradually overlapped with the portrait of a certain legendary name.
"No... he looks familiar. Why does he look a little like Faustus?"
Sean’s voice unconsciously lowered, and an ominous premonition rose in his heart.
However, the Divine-grade powerhouses around him did not possess that same vigilance.
They had already surrounded Daniel in layer after layer, whispering among themselves in disorder, their tones filled with contempt.
"A mere demi-sage rank actually owns such a Holy Relic? Could he be some descendant who secretly slipped out from a major faction?"
"Who cares whose descendant he is? Since he has reached our territory, he has to obediently wait for our judgment."
"Looks like there’s no need for all of us to act together. Just pick two or three sages at random, and they can crush him into powder."
Just as they were whispering among themselves and letting down their guard—
Daniel suddenly raised his hand.
That palm rapidly expanded in the void, like the arm of an ancient giant god awakening from slumber.
In the blink of an eye, that colossal palm covered the void for ten thousand miles around, blotting out the sky and the stars, as though even the stars themselves would be crushed within its grasp.
Within the palm, the star rivers of countless worlds revolved, and the sun and moon flowed in cycles.
It was as if a newborn universe was slowly breathing within it, containing endless destruction and creation.
"Celestial Grasp—!"
Daniel shouted in a low voice. His voice exploded like thunder in the depths of everyone’s soul.

That heaven-covering giant palm came crashing down. Within the miniature Astral Realm in its palm, endless divine power, Immortal Singularity, and fragments of Law erupted like a volcano, unleashing terrifying might capable of tearing apart the star sea.
Rumble!
The giant palm suddenly slammed down.
The many Divine-grade powerhouses of the Council of the Gods roared furiously and unleashed their sage power one after another, each using secret arts as they desperately tried to resist.
However—
Crack, crack, crack...
A series of crisp sounds exploded one after another. Those were the sounds of bones shattering and sage power collapsing, especially piercing in the void.
The Divine-grade powerhouses of the Council of the Gods were forcefully suppressed in place by that giant palm.

Endless Strength swept in from every direction like a tide, grinding them down. It was as though they were not facing a single demi-sage rank, but an invincible army made up entirely of demi-sage-rank existences!
It was as though what they resisted was not the power of one world, but the weight of countless worlds crushing down at the same time.
Under this terrifying force, low-grade sages did not even have time to scream before they were reduced directly to ash.
Mid-grade sages could only barely endure for two or three seconds before their sage power shattered, their sacred bodies collapsed, and they turned into insignificant dust within the star sea.
Only those high-grade sages could barely withstand it for a moment, yet they too suffered heavy Origin injuries in an instant.
Their sage power was like glass struck by a heavy hammer, covered in dense cracks.
Their sacred bodies withered, and their Origin faded, like candles extinguished by a violent gale.
With this one palm from Daniel, several hundred Divine-grade powerhouses were all executed!
[Ding! You have killed a Divine-grade powerhouse, Council of the Gods low-grade sage. You have obtained Origin Crystal × 100 cubic units!]
[Ding! You sold Origin Crystal × 100 cubic units to Doom Guild for 1 copper coin, triggering Millionfold Boost!]
[The sold item is a currency-type item. Please choose quality boost/quantity boost!]
"Quantity boost!"
[Congratulations! You have obtained 1 gold coin! You have obtained Origin Crystal × 100,000,000 cubic units!]
[Ding! You have killed a Divine-grade powerhouse, Council of the Gods mid-grade sage. You have obtained Origin Crystal × 120 cubic units!]
[Ding! You sold Origin Crystal × 120 cubic units to Doom Guild for 1 copper coin, triggering Millionfold Boost!]
[... Repeating process... You have obtained Origin Crystal × 120,000,000 cubic units!]
[Ding! You have killed a Divine-grade powerhouse, Council of the Gods high-grade sage. You have obtained Origin Crystal × 150 cubic units!]
[... You have obtained Origin Crystal × 150,000,000 cubic units!]
System notifications exploded one after another beside Daniel’s ears.
After the fall of several hundred Divine-grade powerhouses, an enormous amount of Origin Crystals dropped. After being enhanced by Millionfold Boost, they all fell into his pocket.
Those cold numbers jumped before his eyes, yet they failed to stir even the slightest ripple in his heart.
Daniel’s strike was incomparably domineering, like the descent of a main god.
Low-grade and mid-grade sages died on the spot. Only a few high-grade sages luckily escaped through the gaps between the fingers of the palm, drenched in blood and in an extremely wretched state.
"Vice Speaker... run!"
"That man... that man is a monster!"
The voice of one surviving high-grade sage was shrill. Cracks continued spreading across his sacred body, and blood gushed out like spring water.
"I have never seen such a terrifying quasi-sage before. He is simply horrifying beyond belief!"
"If I take another strike from him, I will definitely die too! Run!"
Another powerhouse screamed at the top of his lungs, his eyes filled with fear.
Sean had been commanding from afar all along and had not personally entered the battlefield.
At this moment, the sudden change before his eyes left him completely frozen in place.
Several hundred Divine-grade powerhouses.
Several hundred!
Yet they could not even withstand a single palm strike from one quasi-sage?
A name suddenly flashed through his mind like a bolt of icy lightning splitting open the chaos.
Faustus!
The strongest quasi-sage in the current Myriad-Star Cosmos!
