Fuck, this time I suffered a huge loss."
He had originally wanted to seize a Primordial Star Relic, but not only had he failed, he had lost a Sacred Artisan Law Grade secret treasure instead.
This deal had cost him everything!
Daniel and the others were not particularly surprised when they saw that the Divine Sovereign did not chase after them.
A Primordial Law Grade supreme treasure was itself no weaker than an Oracle-grade being.
As long as that Divine Sovereign was not insane, he would know when to retreat.
In the star sea, the existences who lived the longest were often not the ones who fought the best, but the ones who best understood how to judge the situation.
"Congratulations, Boss Faustus."
"Excellent methods, Sir Faustus!"
James, Dustin, and the others all congratulated him one after another, their eyes filled with envy.
"Why didn’t a second Star Relic fly over too?"
Dustin pretended to sigh and shook his head.
"Sir Faustus, that Star Relic was truly fated with you!"
Daniel blinked.
A playful smile appeared at the corner of his mouth.
"I think so too!"
The other powerhouses were stunned and looked at one another.
Daniel smiled.
Now that the Star Relic had already fallen into his hands, it was his.
A star sea treasure land had erupted, and of all things, a Star Relic had just so happened to rush toward him.
This luck was no different from picking up a legendary divine artifact in the wilderness.
Who could truly explain something like fate?
The Shield of Aegis continued traveling through the chaos.
It passed through one dangerous region after another.
In those places, the Chaotic Essence was so dense that it seemed almost tangible.
Within the gray mist, enormous figures could be vaguely seen writhing.
Those chaotic creatures were said to have been born from Chaotic Essence, or perhaps they were the corpses of dead Oracle-grade beings that had developed intelligence again over countless years.
Every single one of them was unimaginably powerful, capable of tearing apart stars with a casual strike!
Fortunately, the Shield of Aegis was a Primordial Law Grade supreme treasure, allowing them to pass safely through that land of death.
After sensing the aura emitted by the shield, those chaotic creatures all retreated like the tide, as if wild beasts had encountered an even more ferocious member of their own kind.
"If we didn’t have this Shield of Aegis, even a Divine Sovereign would probably suffer here."
James looked at the blurry colossal shadows outside, still feeling lingering fear.
"Any one of those chaotic creatures is no weaker than Oracle-grade.
Tearing us apart would be as easy as tearing a sheet of paper."
"The Chaos star sea... is truly incomparably miraculous."
Camille sighed softly.
Her gaze contained both reverence and longing.
The Chaos star sea not only contained secret realms and treasure lands, but also forbidden zones that even Oracle-grade beings did not dare enter lightly.
At this moment, the Shield of Aegis was passing through a special terrain formed by Chaotic Essence.
Countless enormous vortexes slowly rotated in the void, like eyes opening in the depths of the star sea.
They were deep and unfathomable, as if leading to some unknown abyss.
Even a top-tier Divine-grade secret treasure like the Shield of Aegis was affected by the gravity of those vortexes, its speed slowed as it endured an invisible pulling force.
At this moment, it was as though an invisible giant hand was trying to drag it into endless darkness!
Boom—rumble—!
A muffled thunderous sound came from ahead, like the firmament roaring in anger.
Invisible Strength surged over from the distance.
The Shield of Aegis swayed under the tremendous force, like a tiny boat tossed about by raging waves.
The light on the shield’s surface remained as steady as a boulder.
However, Daniel and the others wore solemn expressions, their hearts pounding like war drums.
"Just the chaos of their auras is enough to affect the stability of a Primordial Law Grade supreme treasure..."
James’s voice trembled slightly.
"I’m afraid there are super powerhouses fighting ahead!"
Camille asked curiously, her eyes filled with both fear and excitement.
The answer was soon revealed.
As the Shield of Aegis continued forward while shaking, everyone saw intense fluctuations in the distance.
Space itself looked like torn cloth, revealing pitch-black nothingness behind it.
Daniel extended his mind power like an invisible thread into the depths of that chaos.
Soon, his mind power touched two figures.
They were two existences without the slightest aura leaking outward.
They floated silently in the void, like two divine statues forgotten at the end of time.
There was no light flowing across their skin.
Not even the slightest trace of life fluctuation could be sensed from them.
Even their breathing seemed to have stopped entirely.
If he had not seen them with his own eyes, he would never have believed they were living beings!
"Their divine energy is completely restrained..."
Daniel murmured in a low voice, his tone filled with shock.

"If hiding one’s aura and disguising oneself as a mortal is already the limit, then to restrain all of one’s divine energy and all law fluctuations until one seems like a dead object... just what kind of Rank is this?"
Even if they were standing right in front of him, without special methods, he probably would not be able to detect that they were still alive at all!
"Oracle-grade."
Dustin’s expression changed slightly, and his voice subconsciously lowered.
"And... they are great Oracle-grade beings!"
"Only supreme powerhouses who have stepped into that domain can restrain their auras to such a degree—as if they were death itself, silent, cold, and impossible to peer into."
"Great Oracle-grade beings... are fighting!"
James trembled all over, yet his eyes were fixed firmly in that direction.
The two confronting figures were reflected in his pupils.
"By the Creator God, I’m actually seeing two great Oracle-grade beings fighting to the death with my own eyes!
A scene like this might not be encountered even after drifting through the Endless Starsea for an entire lifetime!"
"In a battle between great Oracle-grade beings, even the aftershocks alone are enough to kill Divine-grade powerhouses."
Daniel sucked in a breath of cold air.
His throat felt dry, as if an invisible hand had clenched around his neck.
Every time those two figures attacked, the fluctuations spread outward from them for millions of miles.
Wherever they passed, stars shattered, the void collapsed, and even Chaotic Essence was torn to pieces.
How terrifying!
The Shield of Aegis struggled through the gaps between the fluctuations, like a lone boat fighting to survive in a storm.
The snake-haired demoness relief on the shield’s surface flickered between bright and dim, as if it too was enduring tremendous pressure.
Only after an unknown amount of time did that forbidden region finally fall far behind them.
Only then did everyone inside the shield slowly let out a breath of relief.

chapters.title: Chapter 328 -328-The Struggle Between Order and Chaos
paragraphs: No one knew how much time had passed.
At long last, the Shield of Aegis finally broke free from that deadly forbidden zone!
Inside the shield, Daniel and the others remained silent for a long time, still lost in the lingering shock of having witnessed two mighty Oracle-grade beings fight each other to the death.
That world-destroying power was branded deep into their souls, leaving them unable to calm down even after a long while.
"So... even those lofty Oracle-grade beings will fight like ordinary mortals in the Star Sea, drawing blades against one another for the sake of profit."
Daniel’s gaze was profound.
"Before the Star Sea, even Oracle-grade beings are nothing more than slightly stronger ants."
"Hahaha... You’re absolutely right. As of now, no existence can clearly describe just how vast this universe truly is. At least, none exist within the understanding of us Chaos Humans!"
"Oh, right. In a little while, we should be arriving at the Chaosverse."
Dustin laughed, his tone much more relaxed than before.
"I heard the Chaosverse is a universe that was born not long ago. Lord Dustin, what exactly is the difference between a newly born universe and our Myriad-Star Cosmos?"
James leaned forward slightly, curiosity flashing in his eyes.
Daniel also listened with full attention.
Although he had read through some ancient texts regarding the Chaosverse, how could those dry written records compare to Dustin, a native of that place, personally explaining it to them?
Dustin looked around at the group. Seeing the interest written clearly on their faces, he cleared his throat and slowly began.
"Since all of you are curious, I’ll give you a brief introduction to the Chaosverse."

"The Chaosverse has existed for only tens of billions of years. Compared with an ancient universe like the Myriad-Star Cosmos, which has existed for trillions of years, the difference between them is naturally as vast as heaven and earth."
He smiled.

"For example, in the various starfields of the Myriad-Star Cosmos, there are more or less one or two dominant-level forces presiding over each region. Order is maintained, and every force keeps to its place."
Daniel and the others nodded silently.
Gold Holy Mountain was the one and only overlord of the Canaan starfield, while Starvault Sanctum was the towering pillar of the Budelica starfield.
These two great forces each guarded their own domain. If foreign enemies dared to invade, they would inevitably be met with a crushing counterattack.
That was the rule.
It was an iron law forged through countless years of slaughter and bloodshed.
"But the Chaosverse is completely different—there, everything is chaos. There are no rules."
Dustin blinked, his voice carrying a trace of helplessness.
"The only truth in the Chaosverse is this: rules themselves have never existed."
Dustin’s voice was low and calm.

"Within each major starfield, wars never cease. Between starfields, endless slaughter continues without pause. Even the forces from outer universes and the native powers of the Chaosverse have never stopped crossing blades."
"Even Oracle-grade beings often fall in the depths of the starry sky. It is so chaotic that with every dawn, some force is uprooted completely, leaving not a single blade of grass behind!"
Daniel and the others could not help but draw in a cold breath.
What kind of universe was this?
It was clearly a hell where law and order had no place to exist!
Yet Dustin’s expression remained relaxed, his tone calm and indifferent.
"However, the situation has improved somewhat now."
Everyone held their breath, afraid they might miss even half a word.
"The current Chaosverse is divided into two great factions."
Dustin’s gaze was as deep as the starry sky.

"The first is called the Order faction. Its members are all native forces and ancient races of the Chaosverse. They advocate imitating the ancient universes, using strength as the foundation to establish boundaries, with each side guarding its own territory and refraining from violating the domains of others."
"We Chaos Humans are members of the Order faction!"

"The second is called the Chaos faction. Its members are mostly invading forces from outer universes. They believe in only one creed—the strong devour the weak. Only those with strength have the right to create the future. Those who fall are unworthy of possessing anything."
Daniel nodded slightly. In his heart, he already understood.
What the Order faction desired was to use Strength as the foundation to divide territory, creating a world like the Myriad-Star Cosmos—orderly, stable, and with every force in its rightful place.
The creed of the Chaos faction, however, was incomparably brutal.
Survival itself was the only justice!
The conflict between these two sides was like blazing fire meeting freezing ice. There was no possibility of reconciliation.
"Then what is the current situation like?" James asked.
"The two great factions are locked in a stalemate."
Dustin shrugged, his tone carrying a faint, helpless sigh.

"After all, the Chaosverse is still a newborn universe. Even if it has remained chaotic for tens of billions of years, that is still only natural. Order is never born overnight. It must be watered by endless blood, and its long road must be paved with the bones of generation after generation."
"If we want to bring order to the entire Chaosverse, we Chaos Humans still have a very long road ahead of us. But we will never yield, and we will never lose our way!"
"You Chaos Humans certainly have confidence and conviction!"
James said with a grin, though a bit more sincere respect had appeared in his eyes.
A chaotic universe meant endless casualties and sacrifice.
Since the Chaos Humans lived amid such chaos, they naturally had no way to remain untouched by it.
Dustin smiled, then turned his gaze toward Daniel.

"Although the Chaos Humans are ranked only third among the human branches of the Endless Starfield, in terms of potential, we are absolutely no weaker than the Saint Lun Humans, who are ranked first."

"Because we took root and sprouted in the cruelest soil. We were tempered and forged in the bloodiest storms. Every single one of our powerhouses crawled out from mountains of corpses and seas of blood!"
The powerful figures present suddenly understood.

The human race was merely a quasi-first-rate race within the Endless Starfield. Whether it was the Myriad-Star Humans or the Chaos Humans, they were only one branch within the great surging river that was humanity.
But every branch would one day flow into the boundless ocean!
As for who would ultimately guide the direction of that current, that would still depend on whose fists were harder!
While the powerful figures were chatting and laughing, the Shield of Aegis had already quietly approached the edge of the Chaosverse.
The transparent cosmic barrier stood right before their eyes, separating the two universes like a soap bubble. It emitted a faint, shimmering glow.
Buzz—!
The edge of the Shield of Aegis cut open a deep rift and steadily sailed into the territory of the Chaosverse.
Dustin suddenly raised his hand and summoned a flag from the void.
The flag unfurled in the wind, embroidered with the ancient emblem of the Chaos Humans.
It depicted a colossal starry-sky beast with its head raised in a roaring posture. The flag snapped and fluttered amid the stars, flying alongside the Shield of Aegis.
"What is that for?"
Camille asked in confusion.
"You’ll know in a moment."
Dustin smiled and shook his head, a hint of caution in his eyes.
"The Chaosverse..."
Daniel, however, paid no attention to these minor details.
His gaze pierced through the shield’s barrier and turned toward this strange, unfamiliar universe.
"The Chaos Humans..."
Dustin guided the Shield of Aegis forward slowly. The shield moved with perfect stability, as though traveling over flat ground.
Daniel and the other powerhouses silently observed this unfamiliar universe. Everywhere they looked, there were unfamiliar stars and unfamiliar lights.
However, they were all powerhouses of the new generation, and their horizons were broad. To them, the Chaosverse did not seem all that different from the Myriad-Star Cosmos.
In the end, it still followed the same divisions of galaxies, star rivers, and starfields.
The stars were still stars.
Only their arrangement was slightly different.
Suddenly, the Shield of Aegis arrived at a certain place.
Boom!
Rumble!
Deafening sounds of collision and explosion came from up ahead. Mixed among them were the thunderous sounds of battle, the screams of the dying, and furious roars filled with rage.
They had...
They had barged straight into a battlefield!?

chapters.title: Chapter 329 -329-Traversing Chaos and Arriving at the Destination
paragraphs: Within this star system, two groups of powerhouses were locked in a battle so fierce that heaven and earth seemed to lose all light!
Their attacks nearly covered the entire star system. Powerhouses kept crashing down amid the fighting, while blood and flames intertwined into an incomparably tragic scene, shocking to behold.
Gradually, one side began to gain the upper hand. Like rising seawater, they pressed toward their opponents with unstoppable momentum.
The Shield of Aegis suddenly came to a halt!

An invisible no-flight formation firmly trapped it in place. Strength from all directions surged like countless unseen giant hands, clutching the shield tightly in their palms and rendering it unable to move.
"A no-flight formation capable of restricting even a Primordial Law Grade treasure..."
Daniel felt a chill rise from his spine.
The one who had laid down this formation was clearly no ordinary figure.
"We can enter, but we can’t leave?"
Camille looked around in confusion, her brows tightly furrowed.
"Once the no-flight formation is activated, every path of retreat is completely sealed off."
James blinked, ready to fight at any moment.
Whoosh, whoosh—!
Just then, two Starships flew over from the distance.
The Starships were painted with the conspicuous emblem of the Order faction.
In the next moment, the hatches of the Starships opened, and a Divine-grade powerhouse flew out, hovering in the void.
"May I ask which force of the Order faction Your Excellency belongs to? Please come out and meet us!"
The powerhouses aboard those two Starships had long since noticed the flag fluttering beside the Shield of Aegis.
That was none other than the sacred flag of the Order faction, a pass that allowed one to travel through the Chaosverse!

If not for that, even with the protection of the Shield of Aegis, any attempt to forcefully barge through this no-flight formation, which was powerful enough to seal off a star system war, would likely have resulted in them being drowned beneath countless attacks.
Swish—!
A stream of light flew out from within the shield, revealing Dustin’s figure.
He bowed slightly, his posture calm and composed.
"Dustin of the Chaos Humans greets everyone."
"So it is the prodigy of the Chaos Humans, the strongest quasi-Sage in our Chaosverse."
The wariness on the Divine-grade powerhouse’s face immediately relaxed, and a smile appeared.
"Passage authority has been opened for you. You may pass freely."
"The path ahead has also been cleared. Please proceed without worry."
Dustin nodded slightly, then suddenly asked, "Has the battle ended?"
"More or less."
The Divine-grade powerhouse waved his hand, his tone relaxed.
"It was only a medium-sized force from an outer universe. We chased them all the way here, and now all that remains is to clean up the battlefield."
"Those bastards from the Chaos faction didn’t manage to escape. Not a single one."
"So that’s how it is. Thank you for your hard work!"
"All for the order of the universe!"
The two exchanged salutes. Afterward, Dustin returned to the Shield of Aegis and continued guiding the sacred shield forward.
Inside the world within the shield.
"So that sacred flag has such a use."
James rubbed his chin, looking thoughtful.
"The Chaosverse is filled with disorder. We could run into the flames of war at any moment."
Dustin explained, "The sacred flag is used to distinguish friend from foe, and it also makes it easier to open passage authority on the battlefield."
"Without this flag, we would have been treated as enemies and shot down long ago."
"What if we run into the Chaos faction, then?"
Camille blinked.
"Then we leave it up to fate."
Dustin’s tone was relaxed, but there was not the slightest hint of a smile in his eyes.

"The two factions are as incompatible as water and fire. Once they encounter each other, it is a Fight to the Death. There is no negotiation, no compromise—only when one side has completely fallen can the other side leave."
Hiss—!
The powerhouses drew in deep breaths.
Only at this moment did they truly understand the weight of the word "chaos" in Dustin’s mouth.

This was a universe forever steeped in slaughter, like a dark forest that would never see dawn. Every traveler had to keep the sword in their hand tightly gripped at all times, not daring to relax for even a moment.
The Shield of Aegis continued flying forward.
But before it had gone very far—barely two star rivers away—it ran straight into another war.
It was once again a fierce battle between the two great factions. Only this time, it was the Chaos faction that held the upper hand.
The powerhouses of the Order faction had been slaughtered almost to the last, their corpses scattered across the starry sky.
Daniel watched helplessly as an Oracle-grade powerhouse from the Order faction fell beneath the sword of an Oracle-grade from the Chaos faction.
Swish, swish—!
The powerhouses of the Chaos faction turned their gazes toward the Shield of Aegis, their eyes filled with playfulness and greed.
"Look at that. It’s even carrying the sacred flag of the Order faction."
"Oh? That’s actually a Primordial-tier Divine-grade secret treasure."
"Attack together! Break that shield!"
On the Chaos faction’s side, there were countless supreme-grade powerhouses, tens of thousands of Divine-grade powerhouses, and even several Oracle-grade beings.
When so many powerhouses attacked at the same time, just how terrifying was that scene?
Countless skills converged into a vast sea of skills, surging toward the Shield of Aegis with overwhelming force.
"Prepare yourselves. We’re breaking out!"
Dustin let out a cold laugh.
This was no ordinary Primordial-tier Divine-grade secret treasure. It was a Primordial treasure—the very ceiling of the Primordial tier!
It could absolutely withstand attacks of this intensity. At the very least, enduring several waves would not be a problem.
He guided the Shield of Aegis and activated it to its absolute limit.
The sacred shield suddenly expanded hundreds of times over, transforming into an ancient sacred shield as towering as a mountain.
Its entire surface was enveloped in radiant armor of light. It traveled safely through the enemy’s sea of skills and charged forward with brute force.
Boom, boom, boom—!
The nearby Divine-grade powerhouses were like clay dolls, smashed to pieces by the impact of the Shield of Aegis.
Whoosh—!
In the blink of an eye, the Shield of Aegis broke through the encirclement, its speed suddenly soaring.
"That was truly dangerous."
After escaping the war zone, James let out a long breath of relief.
One had to know that several Oracle-grade beings had attacked just now. It was only because this Primordial treasure was far too exceptional that it had forcibly endured everything.
"Indeed. Hahaha..."
Daniel suddenly laughed softly.
"This Chaosverse truly lives up to its name. The flames of war stretch on without end. A situation like this has its own kind of grandeur."
"This kind of thing is far too common in the Chaosverse."
Dustin gave a bitter smile and shook his head, his tone carrying the calm indifference of someone long accustomed to battle.
"In this star sea, today’s fierce battle will vanish like passing clouds by tomorrow!"
Black Wasteland Star River.
The Shield of Aegis finally came to a stop, and Dustin put it away.
The five powerhouses appeared, standing in the void.
"Half of the life-bearing worlds in the nearby star systems are frontline headquarters of our Order faction. For the time being, this place can still be considered safe."
Dustin raised his hand and pointed into the distance as he explained.

"The Astral Realm is close to the edge of the Daquan System. Most of the powerhouses coming to participate in the opening of the Astral Realm this time will likely replenish their supplies and rest here."
"In that case, the other half of the star river is the lair of the Chaos faction?"
A trace of emotion flashed through James’s eyes.
Even in this newborn land of the star sea, the shadow of war had never faded!
Daniel and the other powerhouses followed Dustin to one of the great worlds.
"This world is called Donsiri."
Dustin said, "There are many high-grade residences here. Let’s find a place to settle down first."
Sure enough, Daniel and the others soon saw an elemental sacred land.
The elemental power between heaven and earth was so dense that it had almost condensed into substance. Even the flowers and grasses in the garden radiated vigorous vitality.
Some elemental sacred lands like this were occupied by powerhouses, while others were rented out to outsiders.

Daniel and the other powerhouses rented one sacred land together. It was not because they were short on money, but because the Astral Realm was about to open, and the Daquan System was the closest star system to the Astral Realm. Countless powerhouses from outer universes had swarmed in, and all the vacant sacred land residences had long since been seized.
Even the one before them had been rented by the Chaos Humans’ force on a long-term basis.
If they had not prepared in advance, they probably would not even have had a decent place to stay!
A spatial formation had been arranged within the sacred land, so it did not feel crowded.

After painstakingly crossing the Chaos Star Sea all the way from the Myriad-Star Cosmos and witnessing countless wondrous sights, the five powerhouses finally settled down peacefully in Donsiri World.

sentences.text: Within this star system, two groups of powerhouses were locked in a battle so fierce that heaven and earth seemed to lose all light!
Their attacks nearly covered the entire star system.
Powerhouses kept crashing down amid the fighting, while blood and flames intertwined into an incomparably tragic scene, shocking to behold.
Gradually, one side began to gain the upper hand.
Like rising seawater, they pressed toward their opponents with unstoppable momentum.
The Shield of Aegis suddenly came to a halt!
An invisible no-flight formation firmly trapped it in place.
Strength from all directions surged like countless unseen giant hands, clutching the shield tightly in their palms and rendering it unable to move.
"A no-flight formation capable of restricting even a Primordial Law Grade treasure..."
Daniel felt a chill rise from his spine.
The one who had laid down this formation was clearly no ordinary figure.
"We can enter, but we can’t leave?"
Camille looked around in confusion, her brows tightly furrowed.
"Once the no-flight formation is activated, every path of retreat is completely sealed off."
James blinked, ready to fight at any moment.
Whoosh, whoosh—!
Just then, two Starships flew over from the distance.
The Starships were painted with the conspicuous emblem of the Order faction.
In the next moment, the hatches of the Starships opened, and a Divine-grade powerhouse flew out, hovering in the void.
"May I ask which force of the Order faction Your Excellency belongs to?
Please come out and meet us!"
The powerhouses aboard those two Starships had long since noticed the flag fluttering beside the Shield of Aegis.
That was none other than the sacred flag of the Order faction, a pass that allowed one to travel through the Chaosverse!

If not for that, even with the protection of the Shield of Aegis, any attempt to forcefully barge through this no-flight formation, which was powerful enough to seal off a star system war, would likely have resulted in them being drowned beneath countless attacks.
Swish—!
A stream of light flew out from within the shield, revealing Dustin’s figure.
He bowed slightly, his posture calm and composed.
"Dustin of the Chaos Humans greets everyone."
"So it is the prodigy of the Chaos Humans, the strongest quasi-Sage in our Chaosverse."
The wariness on the Divine-grade powerhouse’s face immediately relaxed, and a smile appeared.
"Passage authority has been opened for you.
You may pass freely."
"The path ahead has also been cleared.
Please proceed without worry."
Dustin nodded slightly, then suddenly asked, "Has the battle ended?"
"More or less."
The Divine-grade powerhouse waved his hand, his tone relaxed.
"It was only a medium-sized force from an outer universe.
We chased them all the way here, and now all that remains is to clean up the battlefield."
"Those bastards from the Chaos faction didn’t manage to escape.
Not a single one."
"So that’s how it is.
Thank you for your hard work!"
"All for the order of the universe!"
The two exchanged salutes.
Afterward, Dustin returned to the Shield of Aegis and continued guiding the sacred shield forward.
Inside the world within the shield.
"So that sacred flag has such a use."
James rubbed his chin, looking thoughtful.
"The Chaosverse is filled with disorder.
We could run into the flames of war at any moment."
Dustin explained, "The sacred flag is used to distinguish friend from foe, and it also makes it easier to open passage authority on the battlefield."
"Without this flag, we would have been treated as enemies and shot down long ago."
"What if we run into the Chaos faction, then?"
Camille blinked.
"Then we leave it up to fate."
Dustin’s tone was relaxed, but there was not the slightest hint of a smile in his eyes.
"The two factions are as incompatible as water and fire.
Once they encounter each other, it is a Fight to the Death.
There is no negotiation, no compromise—only when one side has completely fallen can the other side leave."
Hiss—!
The powerhouses drew in deep breaths.
Only at this moment did they truly understand the weight of the word "chaos" in Dustin’s mouth.
This was a universe forever steeped in slaughter, like a dark forest that would never see dawn.
Every traveler had to keep the sword in their hand tightly gripped at all times, not daring to relax for even a moment.
The Shield of Aegis continued flying forward.
But before it had gone very far—barely two star rivers away—it ran straight into another war.
It was once again a fierce battle between the two great factions.
Only this time, it was the Chaos faction that held the upper hand.
The powerhouses of the Order faction had been slaughtered almost to the last, their corpses scattered across the starry sky.
Daniel watched helplessly as an Oracle-grade powerhouse from the Order faction fell beneath the sword of an Oracle-grade from the Chaos faction.
Swish, swish—!
The powerhouses of the Chaos faction turned their gazes toward the Shield of Aegis, their eyes filled with playfulness and greed.
"Look at that.
It’s even carrying the sacred flag of the Order faction."
"Oh?
That’s actually a Primordial-tier Divine-grade secret treasure."
"Attack together!
Break that shield!"
On the Chaos faction’s side, there were countless supreme-grade powerhouses, tens of thousands of Divine-grade powerhouses, and even several Oracle-grade beings.
When so many powerhouses attacked at the same time, just how terrifying was that scene?
Countless skills converged into a vast sea of skills, surging toward the Shield of Aegis with overwhelming force.
"Prepare yourselves.
We’re breaking out!"
Dustin let out a cold laugh.
This was no ordinary Primordial-tier Divine-grade secret treasure.
It was a Primordial treasure—the very ceiling of the Primordial tier!
It could absolutely withstand attacks of this intensity.
At the very least, enduring several waves would not be a problem.
He guided the Shield of Aegis and activated it to its absolute limit.
The sacred shield suddenly expanded hundreds of times over, transforming into an ancient sacred shield as towering as a mountain.
Its entire surface was enveloped in radiant armor of light.
It traveled safely through the enemy’s sea of skills and charged forward with brute force.
Boom, boom, boom—!
The nearby Divine-grade powerhouses were like clay dolls, smashed to pieces by the impact of the Shield of Aegis.
Whoosh—!
In the blink of an eye, the Shield of Aegis broke through the encirclement, its speed suddenly soaring.
"That was truly dangerous."
After escaping the war zone, James let out a long breath of relief.
One had to know that several Oracle-grade beings had attacked just now.
It was only because this Primordial treasure was far too exceptional that it had forcibly endured everything.
"Indeed.
Hahaha..."
Daniel suddenly laughed softly.
"This Chaosverse truly lives up to its name.
The flames of war stretch on without end.
A situation like this has its own kind of grandeur."
"This kind of thing is far too common in the Chaosverse."
Dustin gave a bitter smile and shook his head, his tone carrying the calm indifference of someone long accustomed to battle.
"In this star sea, today’s fierce battle will vanish like passing clouds by tomorrow!"
Black Wasteland Star River.
The Shield of Aegis finally came to a stop, and Dustin put it away.
The five powerhouses appeared, standing in the void.
"Half of the life-bearing worlds in the nearby star systems are frontline headquarters of our Order faction.
For the time being, this place can still be considered safe."
Dustin raised his hand and pointed into the distance as he explained.
"The Astral Realm is close to the edge of the Daquan System.
Most of the powerhouses coming to participate in the opening of the Astral Realm this time will likely replenish their supplies and rest here."
"In that case, the other half of the star river is the lair of the Chaos faction?"
A trace of emotion flashed through James’s eyes.
Even in this newborn land of the star sea, the shadow of war had never faded!
Daniel and the other powerhouses followed Dustin to one of the great worlds.
"This world is called Donsiri."
Dustin said, "There are many high-grade residences here.
Let’s find a place to settle down first."
Sure enough, Daniel and the others soon saw an elemental sacred land.
The elemental power between heaven and earth was so dense that it had almost condensed into substance.
Even the flowers and grasses in the garden radiated vigorous vitality.
Some elemental sacred lands like this were occupied by powerhouses, while others were rented out to outsiders.
Daniel and the other powerhouses rented one sacred land together.
It was not because they were short on money, but because the Astral Realm was about to open, and the Daquan System was the closest star system to the Astral Realm.
Countless powerhouses from outer universes had swarmed in, and all the vacant sacred land residences had long since been seized.
Even the one before them had been rented by the Chaos Humans’ force on a long-term basis.
If they had not prepared in advance, they probably would not even have had a decent place to stay!
A spatial formation had been arranged within the sacred land, so it did not feel crowded.

After painstakingly crossing the Chaos Star Sea all the way from the Myriad-Star Cosmos and witnessing countless wondrous sights, the five powerhouses finally settled down peacefully in Donsiri World.

chapters.title: Chapter 330 -330-Faction War, Divine-grade Cannon Fodder
paragraphs: "I wonder how far the Astral Realm has developed by now?"
There was a hint of inquiry in Daniel’s voice.
"It is already nearing its final stage. In a few more years, it should be ready to open."
Dustin’s tone was calm and gentle.
"A few years will pass very quickly."
"I heard that the Astral Realm only exists for a hundred years. Is that legend true?"
James asked curiously.
"Absolutely true."
Dustin nodded slightly.

"The Astral Realm is a newborn star system, and it will only exist for one hundred years. After a hundred years, all its laws and cosmic mysteries will have evolved to maturity and completion, and the star system will begin to take shape."

"After being washed by the passage of time, this starfield will gradually stabilize and transform into an eternal, indestructible star system. That is why the hundred years in which the Astral Realm blooms are like the brightest morning star before dawn—fleeting, yet brilliant enough to illuminate the entire night sky!"
"In other words, after the Astral Realm opens, we can take away all the essence within it."
"As for whether the chick can break out of its shell afterward, that will be a matter for later."
Camille suddenly understood.
"Exactly."
Dustin continued, "The hundred years from the Astral Realm’s birth to its maturity are an opportunity bestowed upon us by the universe."
The Astral Realm was the initial form of a newborn star system. Only after a hundred years would it grow into a complete star system.
During these hundred years of development, countless opportunities and fortuitous encounters would be born.

Divine-grade powerhouses needed to construct their sage rank, and constructing a sage rank required vast amounts of top-tier precious materials and sacred intent. The Astral Realm contained precisely such supreme opportunities.
Therefore, every time the Astral Realm opened, it would mark a golden age in which top quasi-Sages broke through to the peak of Divine-grade one after another.
The Astral Realm would also attract countless top quasi-Sages from outer universes to come and explore. Even Divine-grade and Oracle-grade beings would be drawn by its radiance!
"What benefits us most is that the first ten years of the Astral Realm are its gestation period. No living being is allowed to enter."
"For the first thirty years after that, only quasi-Sages can set foot inside. Afterward, it will gradually open to Sages, peak Divine-grade beings, and Oracle-grade beings in sequence..."
Daniel smiled.
"In that case, no matter what Rank one belongs to, everyone has the chance to obtain an opportunity that suits them."
The group exchanged their understandings and guesses regarding the Astral Realm.
"This Astral Realm is somewhat similar to the Starlight Rankings tournament back then."
James said thoughtfully, "That tournament gathered nine-star powerhouses from across the entire universe, while this place gathers the most elite quasi-Sages from various universes."
"More or less."
Dustin said softly, "The Astral Realm does not have competition rules. It relies more on opportunity, strength, and teamwork."
"Oh? Is there some particular strategy involved?"
Daniel asked.
"Some opportunities may not suit oneself, but may happen to suit another person perfectly."

Dustin explained, "For example, if I happened upon a fortuitous encounter related to the Law of Causality in the Astral Realm, but I have never cultivated causality arts, then that opportunity would not be very useful to me."
"However, that does not mean it would be useless to you, Faustus. The key is that such opportunities are extremely rare. If you fail to obtain it, it will be seized by other powerhouses!"
"One more friend means one more source of Strength!"
James nodded repeatedly.
Daniel also nodded, falling into thought.
"Since the Astral Realm has not opened yet, shall I take all of you to the war front to have a look?"
Dustin suddenly suggested.
The eyes of the other four powerhouses lit up!
The frontline of the war between the two great factions.
Daniel and the others stopped not far behind the rear lines.
Their field of vision clearly reflected the formations of the Order faction—countless supreme-grade powerhouses had formed one massive army after another, all of them supreme-grade without exception!

Those supreme-grade powerhouses were merely pawns at the front. Although they might have been pillars of talent or prodigies in their own worlds, here, they were only cannon fodder at the very bottom.

Within every supreme-grade army, there were also large numbers of quasi-Sages mixed in. These demi-sage rank powerhouses were at the same Rank as Daniel and the others, yet they could only serve as mid-to-low-level Strength within the army.
Even now, with the Astral Realm about to open, they were not qualified to participate.
Those qualified to set foot in the Astral Realm were all quasi-Sages with extraordinary potential!
Potential was everything!
"Over there is the Divine-grade army!"
Camille cried out in surprise.
Daniel turned his head and looked over.
"Hiss... An army composed entirely of Divine-grade powerhouses."
Daniel’s heart churned with shock.
Back then, a mere low-grade Sage had been enough to firmly block the advancement path of the Aetheria humans.
Yet now, a single army actually contained millions of Divine-grade powerhouses, and they had been reduced to consumables of war just like those supreme-grade beings!
In truth, not much time had passed.
Those Divine-grade beings who had once stood far above him now would not even last a single second in his hands!
"The upper ranks of the supreme-grade armies are Divine Radiant-level powerhouses."
James said calmly, "The upper ranks of the demi-sage rank armies are Divine Sovereign-level powerhouses, and the upper ranks of the Divine-grade armies are Divine Lord-level powerhouses!"
Before a war of this cosmic scale, the supreme-grade armies were cannon fodder in the truest sense, led by a small number of Divine Radiant-level powerhouses.
The demi-sage rank armies were only slightly stronger than cannon fodder, led by a small number of Divine Sovereigns.
The true main force was the Divine-grade army, commanded by a small number of Divine Lords.
Divine Descendant-level powerhouses possessed a great deal of strategic autonomy, mainly targeting the enemy’s high-end combat forces.
As for Oracle-grade beings, they were the key figures who directly determined the outcome of the battle!
"So many Oracle-grade beings..."
Within Daniel’s field of vision, he could see dozens of Oracle-grade beings alone.
Oracle-grade beings were top-level combat forces, capable of directly influencing the direction of the war.
In a cosmic-level war, each faction had dozens of Oracle-grade beings participating in battle. Added together, both sides had more than a hundred.
"And this is still far from the moment of the final decisive battle."
Dustin’s gaze was complicated.

"When the true great battle descends, Oracle-grade reinforcements will continue arriving without end. In a single campaign, it is common to see over a thousand Oracle-grade beings fighting on the same stage."
Hiss—!
Everyone could not help but draw in a cold breath.
What kind of noble existence was an Oracle-grade being?
Yet there were actually over a thousand of them slaughtering one another in war.
The scale of war in the Chaosverse was not inferior in the slightest to an all-out war between universes!
"How tragic."
A trace of sorrow appeared on Dustin’s face.
"Even in wars between universes, there are actually very few occasions where so many Oracle-grade beings take part."
"Yet in a single internal war within one universe, over a thousand Oracle-grade beings can end up slaughtering one another."
His voice was heavy.
"We Chaos Humans have lost quite a number of Oracle-grade beings in this internal war."
Daniel and the others fell silent.
For any race or force, the fall of even a single Oracle-grade being was an immeasurable loss.
As a member of the Order faction, the Chaos Humans were involved in battles where over a thousand Oracle-grade beings fought. It was only natural that some of their combat forces had fallen.
People were bound to die in war!
But war was also the furnace that tempered powerhouses!
The Chaos Humans had grown rapidly amid endless flames of war, and Dustin, too, had been forged within that very furnace.
"The other side also has this many armies and powerhouses."
Daniel’s gaze turned deeply toward the Chaos faction.
The configuration on that side was almost identical to the Order faction’s. After all, these were the only two great powers in this universe.
The combat strength of both sides was evenly matched.

chapters.title: Chapter 331 -331-Nine-Star Prodigies Gather in One World
paragraphs: At a certain moment, the war erupted with a thunderous roar!
"Kill!"
"Slaughter those sanctimonious Order faction bastards!"
"You parasites and tumors of the Chaosverse, welcome the arrival of death..."
The war between the Order faction and the Chaos faction officially began.
For the first time in their lives, Daniel and the others witnessed a scene of such immense scale. Every one of them stared without blinking.
First, the Divine-grade armies erupted, condensing sage rank power that was no weaker than that of a Divine Sovereign. Then, all kinds of treasures poured out in overwhelming waves.
The Divine-grade armies of both sides clashed together, tearing into each other until flesh and blood flew everywhere.
The Divine Descendants also made their moves one after another, engaging in life-and-death battles against powerhouses of the same Rank.
At present, this was only a small-scale operation, so battles at the Oracle-grade level had yet to appear.
Boom!
Rumble!
Seas of skills stacked layer upon layer, and oceans of Sacred Artifacts filled the battlefield densely.
Hundreds of millions of army warriors slaughtered one another in a chaotic mass, their blood staining the void beneath their feet red...
Time flowed by in a hurry.
In the Endless Starfield, time had never been worth much.
Donsiri World.
In the blink of an eye, the time for the Astral Realm to open had arrived!
Several hundred young nine-star powerhouses from various universes had appeared in Donsiri World.
Carrying freshly gathered intelligence, Dustin arrived at the residence of Daniel and the others.
"Lord Faustus, this is the list compiled by my race—the powerhouses who may pose a threat within the Astral Realm."
Dustin spread a roll of parchment across the long oak table, its edges slightly curled.
Daniel looked down, his fingertips lightly brushing across the names.
This intelligence was extremely detailed. It listed several hundred existences with formidable strength, extraordinary talent, and unfathomable potential.
Among them were not only quasi-Sages, but also Divine-grade powerhouses!
Daniel’s gaze finally froze on two names.
"Adonis, Saint Lun Humans..."
Daniel read the name softly.
He knew that among the known human lineages of the Endless Starsea, the Saint Lun Humans ranked first.
This Adonis was the quasi-Sage sent by the Saint Lun Humans to explore the Astral Realm this time. He came from the Saint Lun Universe.
Daniel’s gaze then shifted to another name.
"Aeris, Saintwen Humans."
The Saintwen Humans of Saintwen World ranked behind the Chaos Humans and came from Saintwen World.
Aeris and the others were at the same Rank as Daniel’s group.
In truth, before the rise of the Chaos Humans, the only truly famous human branches had been the Saint Lun Humans and the Saintwen Humans.
Soon, another name on the list caught Daniel’s attention.
[Kain—Valasen Universe, Starbeast, peak Divine-grade!]
"Kain—Starbeast!"
Daniel’s pupils suddenly contracted.
Harris was also a Starbeast, a race hailed as the number one race in the Endless Starsea.
"Harris hasn’t reached adulthood yet and hasn’t awakened his bloodline and inheritance, so he is only quasi-Divine-grade."
Daniel pondered for a moment.
"It seems this Starbeast named Kain has already reached adulthood and awakened part of his bloodline power."
In addition, the parchment also listed powerhouses from many other universes.
The intelligence did not merely include their names, origins, and strength levels. It also included short but precise descriptions of their battle records.
"These people are not weaker than Mosi and me."
James stared at the list.
"Especially among the Divine-grade powerhouses who came this time, there are quite a few particularly dazzling existences."
Dustin shook his head.
"This gathering is no small matter—the Divine-grade powerhouses with Oracle-grade potential have most likely all gathered here."
"These are the most promising Divine-grade powerhouses from the various universes."
Dustin deliberately emphasized the word "potential," as though that word carried the weight of a thousand mountains.
Potential...
Daniel and the others all understood the weight of that word.
If they could successfully break through to the peak of Divine-grade, they would also enter the ranks of those "promising" Divine-grade powerhouses.
In other words, back when the peak Divine-grade powerhouses from the various universes who had come this time were still quasi-Sages, they had likewise reached the nine-star level!
They were the peak among quasi-Sages, the rarest of the rare, like the brightest stars in the vast Star Sea.
"Fortunately, those Divine-grade powerhouses can’t enter the Astral Realm in the same batch as us."
Camille suddenly smiled.
"They have to wait thirty years before they obtain the authority to enter."
"If not for that, wouldn’t we be walking straight to our deaths once we went in? Hahaha..."
James also laughed.
"Thanks to the Astral Realm’s natural restrictions, powerhouses of every Rank have a chance to fight for opportunities."
"Oracle-grade."
Mosi suddenly spoke, his gaze landing directly on Dustin.
Daniel and the others also grew serious.
Indeed, although the Astral Realm’s mechanism gave powerhouses of every Rank a chance, Oracle-grade beings were likewise qualified to enter!
These peak demi-sage rank powerhouses had very high opinions of themselves. Even when facing Divine-grade beings, they felt no fear. If they could not win, they could simply flee.
But if they encountered an Oracle-grade being, even fleeing might not be possible!
The corners of Dustin’s lips lifted slightly, and he gave a soft laugh.
"Not many Oracle-grade beings have come this time. Perhaps it is because the Chaosverse is too chaotic..."

"Most of the Oracle-grade beings from the two great factions of our Chaosverse will enter the Astral Realm. Even if Oracle-grade beings from outer universes come, they may not necessarily be able to gain any advantage against the Oracle-grade beings of the Chaosverse."
"This also means that any Oracle-grade being who dares to set foot here is definitely no ordinary figure."
Daniel and the others nodded slightly.
For the Oracle-grade beings of the Chaosverse, the Astral Realm’s mechanism prevented them from attacking demi-sage rank and Divine-grade powerhouses before the time limit arrived.
But if they encountered Oracle-grade beings from outer universes here, that would be an entirely different matter.
How could the treasures of the Chaosverse be allowed to fall into the hands of Oracle-grade beings from outer universes?

Moreover, life-and-death battles between the Oracle-grade beings of the two great factions were unavoidable to begin with. This kind of risk was likewise extremely high for Oracle-grade beings from outer universes.
Therefore, it was only natural that fewer Oracle-grade beings had come.
"Oh, right."
Dustin grinned, a playful expression appearing on his face.
"Several other nine-star powerhouses from your Myriad-Star Cosmos will also be coming this time."
"Flora, Harris, Udi, Cold Star, and the others!"
James smiled.
"That is within expectations. The Astral Realm has an unimaginable attraction for demi-sage rank powerhouses. They would definitely think of every possible way to get here."
Daniel smiled calmly without commenting.
Several years had passed since the Starlight Tournament.
Now, it was time for them to meet again!
The opening of the Astral Realm itself was an opportunity that could not be missed. No one was willing to stop before the threshold of fate.
"There are still two days before the Astral Realm opens."
Daniel said, "We need to make more preparations."
Everyone nodded.
Dustin, however, did not feel any pressure. With his strength, he feared no challenger, no matter who came.
But James, Mosi, and Camille suddenly felt their shoulders grow heavy, as though an invisible mountain had been placed upon them.
Every powerhouse drawn here by the Astral Realm was no weaker than them!

sentences.text: At a certain moment, the war erupted with a thunderous roar!
"Kill!"
"Slaughter those sanctimonious Order faction bastards!"
"You parasites and tumors of the Chaosverse, welcome the arrival of death..."
The war between the Order faction and the Chaos faction officially began.
For the first time in their lives, Daniel and the others witnessed a scene of such immense scale.
Every one of them stared without blinking.
First, the Divine-grade armies erupted, condensing sage rank power that was no weaker than that of a Divine Sovereign.
Then, all kinds of treasures poured out in overwhelming waves.
The Divine-grade armies of both sides clashed together, tearing into each other until flesh and blood flew everywhere.
The Divine Descendants also made their moves one after another, engaging in life-and-death battles against powerhouses of the same Rank.
At present, this was only a small-scale operation, so battles at the Oracle-grade level had yet to appear.
Boom!
Rumble!
Seas of skills stacked layer upon layer, and oceans of Sacred Artifacts filled the battlefield densely.
Hundreds of millions of army warriors slaughtered one another in a chaotic mass, their blood staining the void beneath their feet red...
Time flowed by in a hurry.
In the Endless Starfield, time had never been worth much.
Donsiri World.
In the blink of an eye, the time for the Astral Realm to open had arrived!
Several hundred young nine-star powerhouses from various universes had appeared in Donsiri World.
Carrying freshly gathered intelligence, Dustin arrived at the residence of Daniel and the others.
"Lord Faustus, this is the list compiled by my race—the powerhouses who may pose a threat within the Astral Realm."
Dustin spread a roll of parchment across the long oak table, its edges slightly curled.
Daniel looked down, his fingertips lightly brushing across the names.
This intelligence was extremely detailed.
It listed several hundred existences with formidable strength, extraordinary talent, and unfathomable potential.
Among them were not only quasi-Sages, but also Divine-grade powerhouses!
Daniel’s gaze finally froze on two names.
"Adonis, Saint Lun Humans..."
Daniel read the name softly.
He knew that among the known human lineages of the Endless Starsea, the Saint Lun Humans ranked first.
This Adonis was the quasi-Sage sent by the Saint Lun Humans to explore the Astral Realm this time.
He came from the Saint Lun Universe.
Daniel’s gaze then shifted to another name.
"Aeris, Saintwen Humans."
The Saintwen Humans of Saintwen World ranked behind the Chaos Humans and came from Saintwen World.
Aeris and the others were at the same Rank as Daniel’s group.
In truth, before the rise of the Chaos Humans, the only truly famous human branches had been the Saint Lun Humans and the Saintwen Humans.

[Kain—Valasen Universe, Starbeast, peak Divine-grade!]
"Kain—Starbeast!"
Daniel’s pupils suddenly contracted.
Harris was also a Starbeast, a race hailed as the number one race in the Endless Starsea.
"Harris hasn’t reached adulthood yet and hasn’t awakened his bloodline and inheritance, so he is only quasi-Divine-grade."
Daniel pondered for a moment.
"It seems this Starbeast named Kain has already reached adulthood and awakened part of his bloodline power."
In addition, the parchment also listed powerhouses from many other universes.
The intelligence did not merely include their names, origins, and strength levels.
It also included short but precise descriptions of their battle records.

James stared at the list.
"Especially among the Divine-grade powerhouses who came this time, there are quite a few particularly dazzling existences."
Dustin shook his head.
"This gathering is no small matter—the Divine-grade powerhouses with Oracle-grade potential have most likely all gathered here."
"These are the most promising Divine-grade powerhouses from the various universes."
Dustin deliberately emphasized the word "potential," as though that word carried the weight of a thousand mountains.
Potential...

They were the peak among quasi-Sages, the rarest of the rare, like the brightest stars in the vast Star Sea.

Hahaha..."

chapters.title: Chapter 332 -332-The Eternal Sage Emerges
paragraphs: Sea of Ruin.
In the depths of the Chaos Starsea, there existed a forbidden land that none below Oracle-grade could touch.
And yet, even Oracle-grade beings could find no true safety here.
A burial ground piled high with countless bones had transformed into an ocean of corpses.
The remains of innumerable Oracle-grade beings lay dormant here, buried through untold ages, through countless eras.
At the end of the Sea of Ruin stood a colossal stone block forged from some nameless substance.
It stretched across a million miles, yet it was not a sealed solid mass.
There was a gate in the stone.
Tap.
Tap. Tap.
Crisp footsteps echoed within.
The sound spread across the entire Sea of Ruin, then rippled outward from that sea of bones, shaking the whole Chaos Starsea.
It was as though an invisible hammer had struck every star.
Tap—!
A skeletal foot stepped out from beyond the gate.
The white bone was crystalline and translucent, with threads of Law power coiling around it like wisps of silk.
The moment that skeletal foot entered the Sea of Ruin, every Oracle-grade corpse in the entire ocean trembled at once, as though welcoming the return of a king who had slumbered for ages.
The Chaos Starsea also began to churn like boiling water set aflame.
Tap—!
The other skeletal foot stepped out of the gate.
In the next instant, a complete skeleton appeared.
Its entire body was as clear and lustrous as jade. Laws wove around it like robes, and endless energy intertwined around its form, giving rise to strange and wondrous changes.
It was impossible to grasp, as though it existed, yet also drifted beyond the universe itself.
At that moment, a hoarse voice slowly rang out, like something rising from the depths of an ancient abyss.
"I, Synros, have finally walked out of that damned place!"
Buzz, buzz, buzz—!
The boundless sea of corpses within the Sea of Ruin suddenly collapsed, transforming into surging tides of countless energies that all poured into the white-boned figure.
Deep within the Chaos Starsea, the hearts of countless powerhouses jolted.
In their subconscious minds, a voice was telling them that some unknown and terrifying existence had descended.
Before that Strength, they were as insignificant as dust, as fragile as ants.
The higher one’s Rank, the more deeply this intuition carved itself into the soul.
The great Oracle-grade beings turned grim, their faces ashen. Their bodies trembled violently, and their lips quivered as they uttered that forbidden name.
"Is... is it the Eternal Sage!?"
The ordinary Oracle-grade beings were so terrified that they knelt one after another in the void, as though doomsday judgment had already descended and the world was about to overturn.
"E... Eternal Sage!"
As for those below Oracle-grade, they did not even have the right to resist that faint trace of aura.
They collapsed to their knees in waves, prostrating themselves toward the Sea of Ruin as though on a pilgrimage.
Deep in their souls, they understood with absolute clarity—
A terrifying existence had appeared.
It was the Eternal Sage, a supreme-grade being standing at the very peak of the Endless Starsea.
At a certain moment, the Sea of Ruin vanished.
Disappearing along with it was the boundless ocean of bones.
That vast tide of Oracle-grade corpses had been completely devoured by the white-boned powerhouse.
At this moment, flesh and blood began to grow over the skeleton, revealing the appearance of a handsome man.
His name was Synros.
His eyes suddenly opened.
The instant he opened his eyes, all events within the river of time across countless years before and after the current era surged into his mind like a tide.
In the blink of an eye, he understood them all.
He tilted his head slightly, casting his gaze toward the Chaosverse.
A faint, unreadable smile rose at the corner of his mouth.
"Interesting..."
Chaosverse.
Black Wasteland Galaxy, Daquan System.
In the nearby starry sky, there existed a strange region spanning hundreds of millions of miles.
Mist-like astral energy lingered around its outer shell, while seven-colored radiance shrouded its surface.
Within it, light flickered endlessly, and mysterious voices echoed like the whispers of ancient gods.
This was the Astral Realm.
A miraculous land about to open, one that contained countless primordial treasures.
Whoosh—whoosh—!
Several streaks of light tore through the void, transforming into the figures of powerful beings.
They stopped silently outside the Astral Realm, quietly waiting for it to open.
Daniel looked around.
Within his field of vision, thousands of powerhouses had already gathered.
Among them were demi-sage rank beings who were about to enter the Astral Realm, as well as Divine-grade powerhouses.
Those sages would still need to wait another thirty years, until the Astral Realm evolved into its next stage, before they could step inside.
"They’re all here."
Dustin spoke to Daniel, his gaze sweeping across the dark mass of figures in the sky.
"The strongest demi-sage rank beings from every major universe. Not a single one is missing."
"Miranda of the Lyra Universe, Vera of the Lunaris Universe, Vincent of the Varasen Universe..."
Daniel calmly swept his eyes over those thunderous names, his tone as still as water.
Every one of these powerhouses stood at the very peak of the demi-sage rank in their own universe.
Each of them possessed strength no weaker than Dustin’s.
In a certain corner.
The many demi-sage rank beings of the Lyra Universe exchanged tacit glances, their expressions carrying traces of hesitation.
Then, one after another, they turned their eyes toward a woman with a cold, aloof bearing and cautiously approached her.
"Lady Miranda, would you be interested in joining forces with us?"
The representative chosen by the demi-sages of the Lyra Universe asked tentatively.
Miranda frowned slightly. Her red lips parted, and she said indifferently,
"Don’t talk to me about interest. Talk payment."
The representative hurriedly said, "You take thirty percent of the gains from the Astral Realm. The rest goes to us."

"There are so many of us. Taking seventy percent shouldn’t be too much, right? Besides, a place like the Astral Realm isn’t somewhere one can go far alone. You need teammates. By yourself, you won’t be able to gain much."
Miranda rolled her eyes and spat out one word with crisp decisiveness.
"Scram."
Elsewhere.
The many demi-sage rank beings of the Lunaris Universe hid far off to one side, staring fearfully at the small figure in front of them.
That figure looked no older than ten or so, her petite body carrying a giant blade even larger than herself.
With her other hand, she kept stuffing divine fruits and sacred herbs into her mouth, her cheeks puffing as she chewed.
Those large eyes seemed adorable at first glance, but from time to time, a chilling sharpness flashed through them.
The powerhouses of the Lunaris Universe consciously kept their distance from her, lowering their voices as they whispered among themselves.
"When the Astral Realm opens, we should try to stay as far away from her as possible."
One powerhouse muttered in a low voice.
"Obviously. We need to avoid her at all costs."
Another shook his head.
"Wherever she goes, we don’t go. In short, we absolutely cannot run into her."
Vera seemed to sense something.
First, she tilted her head and listened for a moment. Then, with a lazy sidelong glance, she looked toward the trembling group of her fellow universe’s powerhouses in the distance.
Hiss—!
The demi-sages of the Lunaris Universe all shuddered at once, their eyes filled with terror. In perfect unison, they retreated several more steps.
"Pfft—"
Vera calmly spat out a fruit pit.
Then she turned back and continued chewing her snacks, though her gaze shifted toward the Myriad-Star Cosmos.
She muttered inwardly,
"I heard Faustus from the Myriad-Star Cosmos is really strong... Wonder how many of my slashes he can withstand. Mm..."

chapters.title: Chapter 333 -333-The Attitudes of the Various Powerhouses
paragraphs: The Varasen Universe camp.
A group of Divine-grade powerhouses surrounded a young-looking demi-sage, all speaking at once as they stuffed all sorts of items into his hands.
"Vincent, are you sure you don’t need the Divine-grade treasures your seniors prepared? One more treasure means one more layer of protection."
One senior spoke with concern.

"Even if you don’t want Divine-grade treasures, at least bring more sacred medicine. Your senior here has quite some attainment in alchemy. Take these potions with you. They might save your life at a critical moment."
"Junior, do you want some rune scrolls? Your senior’s collection can barely be considered presentable. Take a few for self-defense."
Vincent’s hands were quickly filled by his seniors. He gave a helpless smile and retreated again and again.
"That’s enough, really enough... By the stars, there are so many things here that even my storage space is about to protest."

"External objects are ultimately just external objects. What I believe in is using the sword in my own hand to cut through every thorn. Tempering my own strength is the only true path to immortality."
"That may be true, dear junior, but you mustn’t be too stubborn."
A senior sister shook her head, her eyes full of concern.
"The journey into the Astral Realm will be far more dangerous than any trial you have ever imagined!"
"The ones gathered there are not the fellow disciples you usually spar with. Every living being who steps inside carries ambition and strength no weaker than your own."
"That’s right, junior."
Another senior took over, reaching out to pat his shoulder.
"You are indeed invincible within the Varasen Universe. No one of the current generation can contend with you."

"But you must understand that this starsea is far wider than our homeland. The prodigies gathered here now are all ruthless figures who climbed to the top of their own universes by stepping over countless corpses. One more preparation means one more chance to return alive."
"I’ve carefully observed those figures everyone has been paying attention to these past few days: Faustus of the Myriad-Star Cosmos, Miranda of the Lyra Universe, Vera of the Lunaris Universe..."
A man who looked the oldest folded his arms, his gaze as deep as an abyss.

"All three of them carry an indescribable aura. Junior, if you face them, you may not necessarily gain the upper hand. Leaving the others aside, just that Faustus alone—rumor has it that while still at the demi-sage rank, he has already slain a Divine-grade high-grade powerhouse!"
"There’s one more thing, junior. What you hold in your hand is the Scroll of Astral Prosperity, a proof of fate that even Oracle-grade beings cannot forcefully obtain."
Another senior leaned forward and lowered his voice.

"So after entering the Astral Realm, you must remember to first assess the situation in the outer region. Only when the time is ripe should you venture deeper. Do not rush forward out of greed for merit. In the starsea, countless astonishing talents have fallen because of a single word: haste."
"And the final point, also the most important one."
The seniors surrounded Vincent in the middle, all giving their instructions at once.

"Many demi-sage rank beings from our Varasen Universe have come this time. Quite a few of them are your juniors. Although they are not as strong as you, they are still of the same bloodline and origin. If it is within your ability, look after them a little. The starsea is dangerous. Sometimes, the bond between comrades is more precious than any treasure!"
Vincent nodded repeatedly, a helpless yet warm smile hanging on his lips as he hurriedly replied,
"I swear upon my soul, I’ve carved every word of yours into my bones!"
"Rest assured, seniors. I will not disappoint your expectations, nor will I let my sword be shamed."
In another corner.
Jason chatted and laughed with several peak Divine-grade powerhouses beside him, but his gaze would occasionally sweep toward Daniel’s direction.
"That person is Faustus, the invincible demi-sage of the Myriad-Star Cosmos."
Jason pondered inwardly.
"At the same time, he is also the current generation’s peak Starchosen, and Harris’s greatest inner demon!"
Thinking of this, he glanced at Harris beside him.
Jason came from the Starlight Folk, but he had always grown up in the Varasen Universe, while Harris was from the Myriad-Star Cosmos.

The number of Starlight Folk powerhouses was already extremely small, and they usually did not compete for resources in the same universe. This was also Jason’s first time coming into contact with clansmen from another universe.
Through Harris’s description, he had learned of Faustus’s existence.
"This human brat’s talent is unbelievably heaven-defying. It is not inferior to my Starlight Folk at all."
Jason thought to himself.
"What a pity. He is still only a demi-sage. I truly hope he can break through to Divine-grade. At that time, I would really like to test whether his strength is as terrifying as Harris claims."
The corner of his mouth lifted slightly, revealing a meaningful smile.
He was a peak Divine-grade powerhouse, an adult warrior among the Starlight Folk. He had awakened part of his bloodline power and belonged to the very top tier among peak Divine-grade beings.
Harris had yet to reach adulthood. For now, he was merely a demi-sage.
Jason was faintly displeased that Faustus had suppressed the Starlight Folk in the Myriad-Star Cosmos, but he disdained bullying the weak with strength or using age to oppress the young.
As the number one race of the Endless Starsea, he had the pride of a Starbeast!
"Jason, I hope we can enter the Astral Realm together. When the time comes, we’ll have to rely on you to look after us."

"That’s right, Brother Jason. Among the Divine-grade beings of the Varasen Universe, you are practically invincible. Now that Divine-grade powerhouses from so many universes have gathered here, we’ll still have to rely on you to win glory for our Varasen Universe."
"Brother Jason, I heard that many peak sages from other universes have come as well. Do you have confidence?"
Jason smiled.
"Although our Varasen Universe is not exactly united internally, when facing outsiders, we will naturally support our comrades."
"If the Divine-grade beings from other universes dare bully any of you, I will naturally take action. As for those so-called peak sages..."
He paused, and a sharp gleam flashed through his eyes.
"What I enjoy most is challenging the strong, especially those fellows who claim to suppress their generation and call themselves invincible at every turn."
Buzz, buzz, buzz—!
At that moment, a sudden change occurred at the Astral Realm.
The gazes of countless powerhouses were instantly drawn over.
They understood in their hearts that the Astral Realm’s gestation period had ended.
The feast of the demi-sages was about to begin!
The hazy radiance surrounding the outer layer of the Astral Realm suddenly dispersed, like a curtain being lifted by an invisible hand.
Seven-colored light churned and boiled like molten lava. The faint and indistinct voice of the world abruptly became piercing, like the roar of an ancient beast.
"It’s about to begin."
James narrowed his eyes.
"The Astral Realm..."
Camille secretly clenched her fists, only one thought burning in her heart.
This time, I must break through to Divine-grade!
"The Prosperity of Stars."
Mosi’s usually indifferent eyes burned so hot they seemed about to ignite.
"Everyone, stay sharp."
Dustin took a deep breath, raising his guard to the highest level. His entire body was like a fully drawn bowstring.
Daniel nodded.
"Remember to follow the strategy we agreed on. No one is allowed to lose their composure."
"Understood."
"Don’t worry."
The several powerhouses responded one after another, their gazes locked firmly ahead.

sentences.text: The Varasen Universe camp.
A group of Divine-grade powerhouses surrounded a young-looking demi-sage, all speaking at once as they stuffed all sorts of items into his hands.
"Vincent, are you sure you don’t need the Divine-grade treasures your seniors prepared?
One more treasure means one more layer of protection."
One senior spoke with concern.
"Even if you don’t want Divine-grade treasures, at least bring more sacred medicine.
Your senior here has quite some attainment in alchemy.
Take these potions with you.
They might save your life at a critical moment."
"Junior, do you want some rune scrolls?
Your senior’s collection can barely be considered presentable.
Take a few for self-defense."
Vincent’s hands were quickly filled by his seniors.
He gave a helpless smile and retreated again and again.
"That’s enough, really enough...
By the stars, there are so many things here that even my storage space is about to protest."
"External objects are ultimately just external objects.
What I believe in is using the sword in my own hand to cut through every thorn.
Tempering my own strength is the only true path to immortality."
"That may be true, dear junior, but you mustn’t be too stubborn."
A senior sister shook her head, her eyes full of concern.
"The journey into the Astral Realm will be far more dangerous than any trial you have ever imagined!"
"The ones gathered there are not the fellow disciples you usually spar with.
Every living being who steps inside carries ambition and strength no weaker than your own."
"That’s right, junior."
Another senior took over, reaching out to pat his shoulder.
"You are indeed invincible within the Varasen Universe.
No one of the current generation can contend with you."
"But you must understand that this starsea is far wider than our homeland.
The prodigies gathered here now are all ruthless figures who climbed to the top of their own universes by stepping over countless corpses.
One more preparation means one more chance to return alive."
"I’ve carefully observed those figures everyone has been paying attention to these past few days: Faustus of the Myriad-Star Cosmos, Miranda of the Lyra Universe, Vera of the Lunaris Universe..."
A man who looked the oldest folded his arms, his gaze as deep as an abyss.
"All three of them carry an indescribable aura.
Junior, if you face them, you may not necessarily gain the upper hand.
Leaving the others aside, just that Faustus alone—rumor has it that while still at the demi-sage rank, he has already slain a Divine-grade high-grade powerhouse!"
"There’s one more thing, junior.
What you hold in your hand is the Scroll of Astral Prosperity, a proof of fate that even Oracle-grade beings cannot forcefully obtain."
Another senior leaned forward and lowered his voice.
"So after entering the Astral Realm, you must remember to first assess the situation in the outer region.
Only when the time is ripe should you venture deeper.
Do not rush forward out of greed for merit.
In the starsea, countless astonishing talents have fallen because of a single word: haste."
"And the final point, also the most important one."
The seniors surrounded Vincent in the middle, all giving their instructions at once.
"Many demi-sage rank beings from our Varasen Universe have come this time.
Quite a few of them are your juniors.
Although they are not as strong as you, they are still of the same bloodline and origin.
If it is within your ability, look after them a little.
The starsea is dangerous.
Sometimes, the bond between comrades is more precious than any treasure!"
Vincent nodded repeatedly, a helpless yet warm smile hanging on his lips as he hurriedly replied,
"I swear upon my soul, I’ve carved every word of yours into my bones!"
"Rest assured, seniors.
I will not disappoint your expectations, nor will I let my sword be shamed."
In another corner.
Jason chatted and laughed with several peak Divine-grade powerhouses beside him, but his gaze would occasionally sweep toward Daniel’s direction.
"That person is Faustus, the invincible demi-sage of the Myriad-Star Cosmos."
Jason pondered inwardly.
"At the same time, he is also the current generation’s peak Starchosen, and Harris’s greatest inner demon!"
Thinking of this, he glanced at Harris beside him.
Jason came from the Starlight Folk, but he had always grown up in the Varasen Universe, while Harris was from the Myriad-Star Cosmos.
The number of Starlight Folk powerhouses was already extremely small, and they usually did not compete for resources in the same universe.
This was also Jason’s first time coming into contact with clansmen from another universe.
Through Harris’s description, he had learned of Faustus’s existence.
"This human brat’s talent is unbelievably heaven-defying.
It is not inferior to my Starlight Folk at all."
Jason thought to himself.
"What a pity.
He is still only a demi-sage.
I truly hope he can break through to Divine-grade.
At that time, I would really like to test whether his strength is as terrifying as Harris claims."

He was a peak Divine-grade powerhouse, an adult warrior among the Starlight Folk.
He had awakened part of his bloodline power and belonged to the very top tier among peak Divine-grade beings.
Harris had yet to reach adulthood.
For now, he was merely a demi-sage.
Jason was faintly displeased that Faustus had suppressed the Starlight Folk in the Myriad-Star Cosmos, but he disdained bullying the weak with strength or using age to oppress the young.
As the number one race of the Endless Starsea, he had the pride of a Starbeast!
"Jason, I hope we can enter the Astral Realm together.
When the time comes, we’ll have to rely on you to look after us."
"That’s right, Brother Jason.
Among the Divine-grade beings of the Varasen Universe, you are practically invincible.
Now that Divine-grade powerhouses from so many universes have gathered here, we’ll still have to rely on you to win glory for our Varasen Universe."

Do you have confidence?"
