chapters.title: Chapter 334 -334-The Astral Realm Officially Opens -- The Struggle Begins
paragraphs: Everyone present saw the changes taking place in the Astral Realm.
Miranda had already assumed a battle-ready stance, like a leopard coiled to spring at its prey at any moment.

Vera’s chewing sped up by several beats. Her eyes seemed to glow with a faint green light as she stared fixedly at the Astral Realm ahead, looking exactly like a wildcat that had caught the scent of blood.
Vincent also put away his casual, relaxed demeanor. His gaze narrowed into a sharp line.
Boom—!
An earth-shaking roar erupted from the direction of the Astral Realm, as though the entire starsea were trembling.
Mist-like astral energy surged up and down, and seven-colored radiance expanded violently, like a gigantic flower bud in the midst of blooming.
"Now—go!"
Daniel shouted, and his entire body transformed into a streak of light, shooting straight forward.
James, Dustin, Mosi, and Camille followed close behind him. Five beams of light tore through the void so quickly that they did not even have time to leave afterimages.
Whoosh, whoosh, whoosh—!
Almost at the same instant, thousands of demi-sages moved together.
Whoosh, whoosh, whoosh—!
Like a swarm of ignited arrows, they plunged into the Astral Realm from all directions.
The Astral Realm had opened.
"Clear out the outer region first."
Daniel’s speed did not decrease. A sharp light flashed in his eyes.

This was the strategy they had decided on long ago. Only those holding a Scroll of Astral Prosperity could enter the depths of the Astral Realm, and such scrolls were absurdly rare. Even an Eternal Sage could not obtain one out of thin air. It all depended on the favor of fate.
Therefore, the opportunities in the depths could be set aside for now. In any case, very few people could enter.
It was better to sweep the outer region clean first.
As for his teammates, they could scatter and search for treasures on their own.
If they encountered trouble or found something valuable, they could use the special communication items Dustin had given them to call one another.
Those items could both transmit messages and perform fixed-point teleportation, making them extremely practical.
It was said that certain special factions had developed them specifically for unique worlds like the Astral Realm.
Daniel plunged headfirst into the Astral Realm.
Seven petal-shaped planes immediately appeared before his eyes—red, orange, yellow, green, cyan, blue, and violet. Each petal was absurdly vast, stretching across tens of billions of miles.
At the very center surrounded by the seven petals lay the legendary core of the Astral Realm.
He chose the violet plane and flew into it.
The moment he landed, he instinctively spread out his mind power, only for his brows to furrow.
The Laws of the newborn Astral Realm were a complete mess. The moment his mind power was released, it was torn apart and scattered in all directions. He could not detect anything at all.
"So I can only rely on my eyes."
He clicked his tongue. This was a little troublesome.
He had never learned any divine-eye secret arts, nor did he possess any scouting-type treasures.
Thousands of demi-sage rank beings descended into the various planes one after another.
They were all the top ruthless figures of their respective universes. The gap in strength between them was extremely small, and none of them were much slower than the others.
Daniel even saw several demi-sage rank beings from other universes fly past right under his nose.
"I’ll keep a low profile for now and figure out the situation first."
He restrained his exposed killing intent and silently blended into this unfamiliar land like a leopard withdrawing its claws.
"Boss Faustus chose the violet region, so I’ll choose red."
James took out a small disc. Several faint points of light were marked on it, representing the rough positions of his companions.
After calculating Daniel’s location, he turned and flew toward the red plane.
Mosi chose blue, Dustin chose green, and Camille chose cyan.
Those most eye-catching top demi-sages each chose a different color, scattering across the realm like pieces on a chessboard.
Daniel explored the violet land.
He had to admit, the outer region of the Astral Realm was indeed wondrous and dazzling.
The sky was a riot of colors, like an overturned palette.

The earth was rugged and cracked. Between the fragments of landmasses surged chaotic torrents. If one was even slightly careless, they would be swept inside and reduced to nothing, not even bones remaining.
"I also need to be careful of Chaotic Essence."
He slowed his steps and raised his guard to the highest level.
Before long, the sound of fierce combat came from ahead. Thunderous explosions shook the area so violently that even the rubble beneath his feet was jumping.
"Someone’s there!"
Daniel’s eyes lit up. He decisively rushed toward the source of the sound.
At a time like this, people would not easily make a move.
If someone had started fighting, then there was a high chance something good had appeared.
The greater the commotion, the more powerhouses were drawn over.
When Daniel arrived, two demi-sages from different universes were locked in a fierce battle.
These two were worthy of being peak existences in their own universes. The shockwaves from their clash alone were enough to give even a low-grade Divine-grade powerhouse a hard time.
Daniel did not intervene. His gaze swept past them and landed on a seven-colored band of light floating in midair.
The band of light shimmered brilliantly, like a rainbow bridge descending from the heavens.
"That is... the power of Law?"
His eyes suddenly brightened.
To the native beings of this starsea, this thing could improve their comprehension of Laws and had immeasurable value for constructing the sage rank.
But to him, this thing could be converted into divine energy!
He was still far away from his small goal of ten trillion. This was something he had to obtain.
The two battling powerhouses were clearly well aware that this thing would attract the greed of others.
They deliberately expanded their battlefield, enveloping the band of light within the range of their fight.
Anyone who wanted to take advantage of the situation and snatch it would first have to pass through their firepower.
Them fighting each other was one thing, but they would never allow someone else to reap the benefits while they exhausted themselves.
One of them shouted while fighting,
"I’ve already called for support! If you don’t leave now, you won’t be able to leave later!"
"There are plenty of opportunities in the outer region. Do you have to fight me for this one?"
The other sneered.
"You think you’re the only one with support? I called people too!"
"It’s just a strand of Law power. Wouldn’t everything be fine if you handed it over to me?"
"Then it seems there’s nothing to discuss?"
"Nonsense! I clearly saw it first, and you barged in halfway. Now you want to get it for free?"
"Dream on!"
Boom!
Rumble—!
The two fought until their eyes turned red. Sacred light and elemental fragments scattered in all directions.
At that moment, nearby powerhouses arrived one after another, but each newcomer was stopped by those who came after them.
In short, no one was going to obtain that band of Law easily.
Daniel looked at this farce and suddenly smiled.
With a turn of his wrist, a Holy Grail flickering with light appeared out of thin air in his palm—
The Voidbound Grail!
A deep-blue radiance of spacetime Law flowed like ripples along the rim of the grail, exuding an ancient pressure that made even the soul tremble uncontrollably.
Buzz, buzz, buzz—!
Invisible Law ripples spread from the mouth of the grail, like a tear of starlight falling into a silent lake.
The ripples expanded layer by layer, instantly enveloping this entire stretch of heaven and earth.
The dozens of demi-sages present all froze at once and instinctively raised their heads, looking toward the Holy Grail suspended high in the air.
It hovered there quietly, its mouth facing downward, like an inverted dome of heaven—cold, indifferent, and majestic.
Before they could react—
"Celestial Grasp!"
A heaven-covering hand descended from above.

Within its palm, layer upon layer of world projections surged like countless worlds overturning at once. A vast and mighty force stirred up wind and clouds, as though even the void itself would be crushed into powder beneath that hand.

chapters.title: Chapter 335 -335-Divine-Grade Mission, Sacred Grove
paragraphs: "In the name of the gods...!"
One powerhouse’s expression changed drastically, and even his voice went off-key.
"Run! Run now! That Holy Grail is a Primordial-grade treasure—we can’t afford to provoke it!"
The more timid demi-sages had already begun turning to flee.
"What kind of secret art is this? How can it be so terrifying?!"
One powerhouse’s heart trembled as he stared fearfully at the heaven-covering hand. His legs felt as though they had been filled with lead.
"It’s over. We can’t run... Space has been locked down by that cup!"
A powerhouse roared in despair, discovering that the surrounding space had been suppressed into something as solid as an iron plate.
Forget escaping— even the Strength inside their bodies was plummeting rapidly, falling all the way from the peak of demi-sage rank to supreme-grade, then to legendary-grade...
The Law ripples of the Voidbound Grail continued to spread, wave after wave, like an endless tide.

The strength of those dozens of demi-sages was stripped away layer by layer. The more it was stripped, the thinner it became; the more it was stripped, the weaker they became. In the end, they were not even comparable to legendary-grade beings.
And that heaven-covering hand descended like the collapse of the sky, crashing down with overwhelming force.
Rumble—!
The giant palm fell.
The entire land trembled violently, as though it could not withstand that world-destroying Strength.
Dozens of top-tier demi-sages failed to escape.
All of them died instantly!
[Ding! You have killed demi-sage Cohen Blake. You have obtained Origin Crystal ×2,500 cubic units and the Divine-grade treasure Voidbreaker Divine Shuttle (Sacred Artisan Grade) ×1...]

[Ding! You have sold the "Voidbreaker Divine Shuttle" to the Doom Guild, triggering Millionfold Boost! ... You have obtained Origin Crystal ×2.5 billion cubic units and the Sacred Artisan Law Grade treasure Void Divine Shuttle ×1!]

[Ding! You have killed demi-sage rank powerhouse Selena. You have obtained Origin Crystal ×2,650 cubic units and the Primordial-grade Divine-grade treasure Codex of Heavenly Riddles ×1... Millionfold Boost triggered! You have obtained Origin Crystal ×2.65 billion cubic units and the Primordial Law Grade treasure Secret Codex of Heavenly Riddles ×1!]
[Ding! ...]
System prompts flooded into Daniel’s ears, densely packed one after another.
With a single palm strike, dozens of top-tier demi-sages from other universes were directly sent away.
These people were all among the finest elites of their respective universes. Their wealth was far greater than that of ordinary Divine-grade powerhouses.
Daniel not only harvested a large amount of Origin Crystals, but also obtained over a dozen Divine-grade treasures...
And after being multiplied by Millionfold Boost, their quality leapt up by another large margin.
"Opportunities..."
Daniel blinked. A thought suddenly surfaced in his mind.
"Wait... aren’t these demi-sages the greatest opportunities?"
"Hiss... That actually makes a lot of sense."
He reached out and grabbed the seven-colored band of light firmly.
The band of light transformed into countless dazzling motes in his hand, scattering like fragments of starlight.
[Ding! You have obtained divine energy +100 billion!]
Tsk, tsk—!
Daniel was overjoyed.
This single strand of Law power had directly poured one hundred billion divine energy into him.
He was one step closer to his small goal of ten trillion.
"I’ll keep these Divine-grade treasures for now."
He was not in a hurry to inspect them one by one. Time was precious right now, and he could not afford to waste it on that. He could deal with them later.
At that moment, the system prompt sounded again.
[Ding! You have triggered a special mission. Your mission panel has been updated. Please check the details.]
Daniel opened the mission panel.
[Ascend to Sage Rank! Special Mission]
Restriction: Faustus Exclusive
Mission Objective: Become a Divine-grade powerhouse.

Mission Content: The Astral Realm nurtures great opportunities. By breaking through to Divine-grade here, your sage rank can absorb the essence of the Astral Realm and receive an extremely powerful enhancement.
Mission Duration: Long-term.
Mission Description: Forge a supreme sage rank, absorb the essence of the Astral Realm, ascend to the Divine-grade realm, and directly reach the peak of Divine-grade!
Mission Rewards: Thunder elemental core ×1, Metal elemental core ×1, Divine-grade achievement reward...
The instant he saw the mission rewards, Daniel froze completely.
Elemental cores!

These were exactly what he had been searching for all this time. At present, he had already gathered eight elemental cores. He was only missing these final two before he could unseal that supreme codex—
Chronoverse Prologue Codex.
After studying this codex, he would be able to touch the threshold of spacetime Laws.
The Origin structure of the Endless Starsea was composed of the two great Laws of space and time.
Daniel understood better than anyone what that codex represented.
"Breaking through to Divine-grade in the Astral Realm can also allow my sage rank to fully absorb the essence of the Astral Realm?"
He truly had not known about this before.
If not for this mission reminder, he might have planned to break through only after returning.
"I almost lost out on a hundred billion."
That was exactly how he felt right now.
Fortunately, he had not taken the wrong path.
"Besides the elemental cores, there’s also an achievement reward."
Any reward placed together with elemental cores could not possibly be bad.
"As the first player to break through to Divine-grade, it would be a little unreasonable if the system didn’t give me a Primordial Law Grade treasure, right?"
He thought happily, the corners of his mouth refusing to stay down.
"As long as I break through to Divine-grade, my overall strength will rise by another wave."
Light flashed in his eyes.
The top-grade Sacred Materials and divine energy required to forge a supreme sage rank were no small amount. The resources he had accumulated so far were still far from enough.
At that moment—
Beep—!
Beep, beep—!
Something in his arms began to ring.
It was the communication and teleportation item Dustin had given him.
"They found something good."
Daniel’s heart jumped.
The urgent beeping continued to echo from his chest like war drums urging an army forward.
Daniel did not hesitate. He immediately activated the teleportation function.
Whoosh—!
His figure instantly appeared in the cyan plane, and the first thing he saw was Camille.
This plane was similar to the violet plane. It was also composed of land fragments suspended in chaos.

However, this place was also very different. The light here was exceptionally brilliant, as though countless treasures were buried within, illuminating the entire void like a gold-grade heaven among legendary-grade realms.
Within his field of vision appeared a vast Sacred Grove.
Sacred medicines, sacred trees, sacred fruits, sacred herbs, sacred crystals...
All kinds of rare and precious materials filled the area in dazzling abundance, glowing with flowing radiance like a garden personally planted by the Creator.
"How fertile."
Daniel could not help but praise in a low voice, a sharp gleam flashing through his eyes.
His mind power swept across the surroundings, and his brows furrowed slightly.

At the edge of this Sacred Grove stood hundreds of demi-sages packed densely together. Many more streaks of light were still rushing over from afar. Clearly, the powerhouses of other universes were also calling their companions.
This cake was too big.
No one could swallow it in one bite!
Camille walked to his side and lowered her voice.

"My lord, this Sacred Grove has not fully matured yet. No one dares to forcibly harvest it. If anyone acts rashly, the spirituality of these Holy Relics will collapse, and their quality will plummet."
Daniel nodded slightly.
The Astral Realm had just been born. This land itself was a cradle for nurturing supreme treasures.
Forcibly seizing them would only destroy the ecology here.
"Soon."
A burning light flickered in Camille’s eyes as she stared fixedly at those swaying sacred medicines.
"They are about to mature."
Daniel calmly swept his gaze over the hundreds of powerhouses eyeing the grove like hungry tigers.
A cold curve tugged at the corner of his mouth.
Every single precious material in this Sacred Grove was a rare treasure urgently needed to forge his sage rank.
Once they matured—
A bloody storm of slaughter and plunder would erupt.
And he did not mind being the first to raise his knife and fork at this feast.

One powerhouse’s expression changed drastically, and even his voice went off-key.
"Run!
Run now!

You have obtained Origin Crystal ×2,650 cubic units and the Primordial-grade Divine-grade treasure Codex of Heavenly Riddles ×1...

You have triggered a special mission.
Your mission panel has been updated.
Please check the details.]

Special Mission]
Restriction: Faustus Exclusive
Mission Objective: Become a Divine-grade powerhouse.
Mission Content: The Astral Realm nurtures great opportunities.
By breaking through to Divine-grade here, your sage rank can absorb the essence of the Astral Realm and receive an extremely powerful enhancement.

chapters.title: Chapter 336 -336-Decisive Withdrawal, One Man Holds the Pass
paragraphs: The Astral Realm was a newborn world.
Its world will had yet to manifest, and its Laws were still taking shape.
Laws intertwined throughout this newly born heaven and earth, weaving all manner of rare treasures into existence.

There were native sages born from chaos, primordial treasures that had yet to fully form but were already radiating dazzling light, primordial Law power drifting like ribbons, and sacred medicines and sacred fruits swaying from their branches.
Everything in this world was filled with opportunity!
Within the cyan plane at the outer region of the Astral Realm, countless primordial Holy Relics were being nurtured.

Hundreds of demi-sages from the major universes had gathered here. Every single one of them had come to plunder the Astral Realm’s Holy Relics and seize newborn Laws in order to construct their own sage rank.
Right now, that Sacred Grove was like a piece of fat meat. Every wolf present wished they could pounce on it and tear off a vicious bite.
Many powerhouses summoned their comrades over, hoping to claim a share of this feast.
James, Mosi, and Dustin arrived one after another as well.
"More than half of them are here!"
James looked at the densely gathered demi-sages before him, a trace of surprise flashing through his eyes.
"Aeris of the Sanctum Sigil human race from the Sanctum Sigil Universe is here too."
Dustin’s gaze landed on a young man whose entire body exuded an ancient and simple aura.
"I once sparred with him. We were evenly matched!"
Daniel glanced indifferently at Aeris.
The human race had many branches in the Endless Starsea, and the Sanctum Sigil human race was one of the ancient bloodlines with deep foundations.

Aeris was currently the strongest demi-sage of the Sanctum Sigil human race. The fact that he could fight Dustin to a draw was enough to prove that his talent and strength could not be underestimated.
"Harris, Cold Star, Igor, and Udi are here too."
James smiled and immediately spotted the powerhouses of the same Rank from the Myriad-Star Cosmos.
At the same time, not far away, Harris and the others’ expressions changed in unison, as though they had seen a ghost.
"That Faustus has joined forces with Dustin... This is going to be troublesome!"
Cold Star shrank his neck back somewhat warily, his eyes turning quickly.
"And there’s James and Mosi too. With those guys here, we definitely have no chance."
"Damn it. What a waste of time."
Udi spat with an unlucky expression.
"Forget it. Let’s try our luck elsewhere."
Harris sighed, his tone filled with unwillingness.
"Let’s go, quickly."
Igor’s scalp went numb the moment he saw Dustin, let alone the Faustus who had once killed dozens of demi-sages with a single palm strike.
He was afraid that if he continued to participate, he would be left in this unfamiliar land forever.
These demi-sages of the Myriad-Star Cosmos chose to withdraw without the slightest hesitation.
Their actions left some surrounding powerhouses puzzled, and whispers began to rise.
"What’s wrong with them? They came all this way and ran off with their tails between their legs before even plucking a single blade of grass. I bet they’re just as spineless in their own universe."
"I’ve drifted through the starsea for so many years, but this is the first time I’ve seen cowards like this. Look at them. They look like mice that just saw a cat."
"Who knows what remote corner they crawled out from? They’ve completely disgraced the face of powerhouses!"
Dustin let out a soft sound of surprise, his gaze following Harris and the others as they left. His brows furrowed slightly.
He did not understand why those powerhouses from the Myriad-Star Cosmos had fled in panic without even fighting for a chance.
"At least they have brains."
James sneered.
"Saves us the trouble of cleaning out the trash."
"Mm."
Mosi calmly echoed him.
Daniel also could not help but smile, a playful curve rising at the corner of his mouth.
He thought of the outer-universe demi-sages he had just killed with one palm strike. Harris and the others had indeed left at just the right time.
The corner of his mouth lifted slightly.
If those people had stayed behind to fight for the treasures, he would not have shown mercy.
In this starsea, everyone was a naked competitor!
Mercy had never been a virtue of the strong!
The Holy Relics within the Sacred Grove were about to mature.
The mist-like energy churned more and more violently, as though the pulse deep within the earth were beating.
The hundreds of demi-sages present stared greedily at that garden while cautiously guarding against the other powerhouses around them.
In this lawless, savage land, every person beside you could become the enemy who swung a blade at you in the next moment.
"This is a little troublesome. Dustin of the Chaosverse is not simple."
Aeris of the Sanctum Sigil Universe looked toward Dustin with fear in his eyes, his brows locked tightly.
"I can’t act recklessly later. I’ll fish in troubled waters first. If the struggle becomes too intense, I’ll stand back and watch for the time being."
"Only by staying alive does one have the right to speak of gains."
The many demi-sages present were also making their own calculations. Some secretly formed alliances, some exchanged glances, and some silently prepared killing moves.
This situation was destined to descend into chaos!
At a certain moment...
Within the Sacred Grove, the mist-like energy was suddenly drawn in as though by a huge invisible mouth, completely absorbed by those Holy Relics.
Seven-colored radiance blazed like a scorching sun falling into the mortal world.
All the Holy Relics had reached the moment of maturity!
The many demi-sages present were instantly invigorated, fanatic flames igniting in their eyes.
"Charge in!"
"All of you, get out of my way!"
"I’ve taken a liking to that sacred fruit. All of you, back off..."
"Let’s surround this orchard. Whoever dares come near dies!"
Whoosh, whoosh, whoosh—!
James, Mosi, Dustin, and Camille almost simultaneously unleashed their respective Divine Domains.
However, they ignored the demi-sage rank beings whose eyes had turned red with slaughter and instead directly transformed into streaks of light, flying toward the Sacred Grove.
The Holy Relics themselves possessed no weak strength and required them to personally subdue.
As for the hundreds of powerhouses howling as they charged toward the garden, all of them were left to Daniel.
Daniel stood in the void, coldly watching the frenzied demi-sages in his field of vision. A smile appeared at the corner of his mouth.
The hunt had begun!
With a flip of his hand, he took out the Voidbound Grail.
The light of spacetime Law released an ancient pressure, like whispers from the depths of space and time.
"Devour—!"
Buzz—!
In the blink of an eye, the Voidbound Grail expanded until it was as massive as a mountain, blotting out the sky and sun.
Its mouth faced downward like an opened giant eye, coldly overlooking the tiny ants below.
Buzz, buzz, buzz—!
Invisible Law ripples spread from the mouth of the grail, instantly pulling every inch of the void into the Holy Grail’s domain.
The Divine Domains of those hundreds of demi-sages were mercilessly corroded, torn apart, and dissolved by the Law ripples.
Their Divine Domains began to shrink. Their divine power drained away rapidly like sand flowing through an hourglass, and their strength was constantly weakened.
Peak demi-sage, demi-sage, supreme-grade, legendary-grade...
It fell all the way down, as though plunging into a bottomless abyss.
The hundreds of demi-sages discovered in terror that their Strength was about to fall below even the threshold of legendary-grade.
Only a handful of them carried special Divine-grade treasures and could barely resist the Laws of the Voidbound Grail.
Cold sweat covered the foreheads of the hundreds of demi-sages.
"In the name of the gods... what kind of treasure is this?"
"A Primordial Law Grade treasure! Damn it! What kind of monster have we run into?"
"How are we supposed to fight this? We’re almost turning into ants!"
"Run! Run now!"
"Escape!"
"Only an idiot wouldn’t run!"

chapters.title: Chapter 337 -337-Claiming Seventy Percent of the Gains Alone
paragraphs: The greed of the many demi-sage rank beings was instantly swallowed by fear, as though a basin of ice water had been poured over them.
Although there were many Holy Relics inside the Sacred Grove, compared to their own lives, what did Holy Relics even count for?
With their strength weakened off a cliff, they now wished they could immediately leave this damned place and flee as far away as possible.
But—
Bang, bang, bang!
Hundreds of demi-sage rank beings fled to the edge of the land fragment, only to suddenly discover that space had been completely sealed!
It was as though an invisible giant hand had clenched this entire stretch of heaven and earth in its palm.
They could not escape!
The Voidbound Grail could not only weaken a target’s strength, but could even forcibly suppress targets stronger than its wielder.
Daniel could even suppress a sage’s sage rank, let alone these mere demi-sage rank beings.
"Suppress—!"
Daniel shouted in a low voice, immediately activating another power of the Voidbound Grail.
Whoosh—!
A violent gale swept out from beneath the mouth of the grail.
The roaring wind swept past, and almost all the demi-sages were dragged and wrapped up by an irresistible suction force. Like withered leaves caught in a vortex, they were sucked into the Holy Grail.
The gale enveloped the entire land fragment, sweeping this stretch of heaven and earth clean in the blink of an eye.
Just moments ago, hundreds of demi-sages had been sharpening their blades for slaughter.
Now, they were helplessly swallowed by the Holy Grail.
Only a handful of powerhouses managed to hold on under the protection of their treasures.
Yet even they were like flickering candles in the wind, liable to be extinguished at any moment!
Daniel slowly raised his palm.
"Celestial Grasp—!"
Whoosh—!
A heaven-covering giant palm appeared in the void, as though propping open the entire sky.
Deep within its palm, galaxies and starfields manifested layer upon layer, containing a vast and terrifying might.
Boom—!
The giant palm came crashing down like the overturning of the heavens and the fall of the gods.
Even the newly forged space of the Astral Realm could not withstand the might of that giant palm. It trembled faintly, letting out a strained groan as though unable to bear the burden.
"That... what kind of Sacred Art is that..."
Relying on his Divine-grade treasure and his own solid strength, Aeris was barely resisting the suppression of the Voidbound Grail.
Now, seeing that heaven-covering giant palm descending upon him, despair surged from the depths of his bones.
"This is a greater Sacred Art!"
Another surviving demi-sage rank being roared in despair and confusion.
"But... but this greater Sacred Art is far too heaven-defying! This is not Strength a demi-sage rank being should be able to grasp!"
"Damn it... we can’t move..."
The eyes of the few surviving demi-sages were filled only with that giant palm drawing ever closer, as though mortals were looking up at the collapse of the sky.
Rumble—!
Daniel’s giant palm descended with a crash.

The Divine-grade treasures of those demi-sage rank beings were already struggling against the suppression of the Holy Grail. How could they possibly endure the palm force of this greater Sacred Art unleashed to its utmost limit?
One treasure after another was sent flying by the giant palm, tumbling and wailing through the void before turning into ash.
Boom!
The ground rapidly cracked apart. Spiderweb-like fissures spread in all directions, and the entire land fragment trembled.
The power of one palm was terrifying to such an extent!
Daniel withdrew the Sacred Art, his robes snapping in the wind.

The reason Celestial Grasp could erupt with such terrifying might was because he possessed endless energy that could be fully stored within this greater Sacred Art, allowing it to unleash power at an extreme limit.
One of his unique talents was an unparalleled ability to charge energy without limit.
Only the three Sacred Arts—Celestial Grasp, Immortal Icon, and Titan Body—could almost perfectly pour out the full extent of his strength.
Even an ordinary sage would die if faced with this palm strike.
As Daniel withdrew the Sacred Art, densely packed system prompts rang beside his ears.

chapters.title: Chapter 338 -338-Gray Lotus, Uninvited Guests
paragraphs: Listening to the harvest prompts constantly ringing beside his ears, Daniel revealed a satisfied smile.
Among the Holy Relics he had obtained, Sacred Artisan Law Grade items advanced into Primordial Grade, while Primordial Grade items advanced into top-tier Primordial Law Grade!
The gains from this wave, combined with the treasures looted from the hundreds of demi-sages he had killed, had already reached an unimaginable astronomical figure.
"Continue searching the other planes."
He swept his gaze over the group.
There were seven great planes in the outer region of the Astral Realm. Naturally, they could not all gather in one place. That would be a waste of manpower.
"Understood!"
"Let’s move!"
Whoosh—whoosh—whoosh—!
Several figures transformed into streaks of light, shooting toward their respective planes.
The original violet plane.
The moment Daniel landed inside, he felt the surrounding mist surge and churn. His vision became hazy and indistinct, as though he had fallen into a forgotten dream.
There were almost no traces of other powerhouses here. A strange silence filled the air.
"Illusion?"
Daniel’s eyes lit up, and the corner of his mouth rose slightly.
His intuition told him that beneath this mist, there was a high chance something extraordinary was hidden.
"Clearstone!"
He activated this Holy Relic without the slightest hesitation.
This treasure was naturally capable of countering all illusion and bewilderment arts, and the current situation was merely one form of illusion.
Whoosh!
Daniel’s vision suddenly changed.
The mist retreated like a tide, and everything before him became clear.
In the sky, a water lily was slowly blooming.
It was a gray water lily, its petals layered upon one another, dark and profound, as though it had grown out from the depths of chaos itself!
Faint mist-like energy wrapped around it, while seven-colored radiance intertwined and tangled together, transforming into wisps of gray energy that nourished the water lily like milk.
"Law power transforming into Chaotic Essence? Chaotic Essence is actually nourishing this water lily..."
Daniel’s pupils suddenly contracted.
"Could this Holy Relic be... a Primordial Law Grade treasure?"
He could not help but draw in a cold breath.
This meant that the starting grade of the Gray Lotus before him had already surpassed his Voidbound Grail!
"The key is... what exactly is this thing?"
Daniel could not recognize it.
That Gray Lotus had clearly not matured yet, but it was close.
This place had previously been protected by an illusion array, and no powerhouse had discovered its existence. Right now, he was the only one here.
He was not in a hurry. He planned to quietly wait for the Gray Lotus to mature before making his move to harvest it.
"This water lily doesn’t seem like a Divine-grade treasure."
Daniel murmured thoughtfully, his gaze deep.
"Instead, it seems more like a Law aggregate derived from Law power... In that case, this thing is very likely—Law Essence!"
Thinking of this, Daniel’s breathing quickened slightly.
"Something like Law Essence has always only existed in ancient legends, and its forms are ever-changing."
He recalled the ancient texts he had once read in Ivahpin World, light flickering in his eyes.
"According to legend, when Law Essence matures, the voice of the world will crown it. That sound is like the sigh of an ancient god, yet also like the first cry of the universe at its birth."

"Once absorbed, it can grant a leap-like improvement to the Law power within one’s sage rank. And at the moment Law Essence matures, it will also release countless Law fragments. Those fragments provide immeasurable assistance in tempering divine energy and condensing the foundation of a sage rank!"
"So... in the outer region of the Astral Realm, Law Essence is absolutely the most top-tier and rarest fortune of all. There is no equal!"
At this thought, Daniel felt as though his blood were boiling.
"By the stars, my luck is ridiculously good. Even the Goddess of Fate must be favoring me."
At that moment—
Whoosh! Whoosh! Whoosh!
Several figures suddenly descended from the sky and landed nearby.
When they set foot in this stretch of heaven and earth, their eyes still carried a trace of confusion. They had yet to recover from the discomfort of spatial travel.
"Huh? Why has the mist here dispersed?"
"Strange. When I passed by this place just now, I clearly couldn’t see my own hand in front of my face. How did the clouds suddenly clear in the blink of an eye?"
"Wait... what is that gray water lily?"
The three demi-sages all turned their gazes toward the Law Essence at the same time—
The Gray Lotus quietly blooming there.
With just one glance, they were deeply drawn in. Their gazes could no longer move away, as though their very souls had been sucked into that lotus.
Among them was a human powerhouse from the Saint Lun Humans—
Adonis!
The expression on his face slowly changed from confusion to shock, then to wild joy, like a traveler who had been thirsty for three days and nights in the desert suddenly seeing an oasis.
However, in the next instant, his face darkened abruptly.
"To think it is Law Essence... Fate has actually favored me so greatly."
The corner of Adonis’s eye caught sight of Daniel’s figure. His eyelid twitched violently, and icy killing intent burst from his eyes.
At the same time, killing intent also rose in his heart toward the two fellow demi-sage rank beings beside him!
These two nuisances had to be dealt with as well!
"This Law Essence is mine. No matter who stands before me, they must die."
As for the two comrades beside him, they became wary of Daniel.
The Gray Lotus before them was clearly extraordinary at first glance, and Daniel was the only stranger from an outer universe here.
They could only blame his bad luck for coming here alone.
The more people who knew of the treasure’s existence, the more variables there would be.
Of course he had to be killed!
"Hmm?"
Daniel looked indifferently at the three powerhouses who had just appeared, the corner of his mouth tugging into an icy curve.
"Are they... targeting me?"
"Heh."
Those three powerhouses all came from the Varasen Universe.
The strongest among them was Adonis of the Saint Lun Humans.
They made no attempt to hide the hostility and killing intent they were releasing toward Daniel.
However, both sides tacitly chose not to summon their teammates.
Daniel had never encountered an opponent in his own rank and naturally did not need help.
Adonis understood the value of Law Essence. He had even developed killing intent toward demi-sage rank beings from the same universe, so he would certainly not create more trouble for himself.
Only the two demi-sage rank beings who could not see through the origins of the Law Essence remained wary of Daniel while asking in low voices,
"Lord Adonis, what kind of treasure is this thing? It looks extremely extraordinary!"
"The ancient records of your Saint Lun Humans should have some mention of it, right?"
"That’s right. Our races are weak and far inferior to the Saint Lun Humans. Would you be willing to explain it to us?"
Killing intent surged in Adonis’s heart.
Two pieces of trash!
Why should I tell you?
"This thing..."
He pretended to be puzzled and shook his head, his tone carrying just the right amount of confusion.
"The ancient records of my race are as vast as the ocean. I have not happened to read any records concerning this object."
"Perhaps... it is merely a relatively rare Holy Relic, nothing worth making a fuss over."
As he spoke, he secretly gripped a Divine-grade treasure, quietly accumulating Strength without revealing anything.
In his mind, two thoughts tangled and bit at each other like venomous snakes.
Should he first kill the comrades beside him and remove the obstacles?
Or should he first slaughter that outer-universe demi-sage rank being who had come alone, then turn back to deal with these two nuisances?

chapters.title: Chapter 339 -339-Crushing the Saint Lun Prodigy, World Essence
paragraphs: Daniel’s perception was incomparably sharp.
The killing intent emanating from those three was like phosphorescent fire in the dark, instantly caught by him.
"How could I allow hyenas to bare their teeth and lick blood over something I’ve set my eyes on?"
A surge of displeasure rose in his heart.
And they even dared to target me?
Then use your lives to atone for that arrogance.
Daniel had never been one to hesitate.
Whether the treasure had yet to mature, whether it might alarm others—he did not care about any of these concerns.
Any enemy he wanted to suppress would simply...
Die!
Whoosh, whoosh, whoosh...!
Ninety-nine clones suddenly stepped out from the void, surrounding the three powerhouses from the Varasen Universe.
Every clone was identical to his true body, their eyes cold and their auras deep, as though ninety-nine gods of death had opened their eyes at the same time.
At the same time, he flipped his hand and took out the Voidbound Grail.
The Holy Grail rose into the air, and deep-blue light of spacetime Law instantly enveloped this stretch of heaven and earth.
"Titan Body!"
"Immortal Icon!"
The ninety-nine clones roared in unison.
Their bodies rapidly expanded, transforming into ten-thousand-meter giants that stood between heaven and earth, like ancient titans walking out from legendary-grade myth.
Their shadows covered the entire land, shrouding Adonis and the others in darkness.
The Voidbound Grail hung high in the sky, overlooking the ants that were about to be crushed.
Law ripples spread outward in rings, sealing space, draining Strength, and grinding the enemies’ battle intent into dust bit by bit.
"Not good! Attack now!"
Adonis suddenly recovered from his shock, his voice carrying traces of hysteria.
"Kill!"
The other two demi-sage rank beings were also stunned that Daniel had actually dared to strike first.
The treasure had not even matured yet. Wasn’t he being far too impatient?
Was he not afraid of destroying this blessed land?
Ninety-nine titan giants attacked in unison. Their sky-covering fists descended with world-destroying might.
The demi-sages from the Varasen Universe hurriedly summoned their Divine-grade treasures to counterattack or barely defend themselves.
However, under the Law ripples of the Voidbound Grail, their strength had already been weakened off a cliff. They still wished to resist, but they no longer had the power to fight back.
The immense strength of Daniel’s clones instantly tore through space, and countless attacks came crashing down from all directions.
Boom!
Rumble!
The clones directly clashed with the three’s attacks, fist meeting flesh, every blow accompanied by the grating sound of bones shattering.
The weakened demi-sage rank beings had no ability to resist.
Almost in an instant, the two comrades did not even have time to scream before they were smashed into powder.
Adonis used all his strength and brought out his final life-saving treasure, but it only allowed him to hold on for a few more seconds.
Then, several giant fists landed on him at the same time, blasting him and that treasure into fragments that scattered through the void.
Daniel had always relied on incomparably sharp attacks and an endless supply of Strength to sweep through everything.
And now, he also held a top-tier Divine-grade treasure like the Voidbound Grail.
Against any powerhouse of the same Rank, as long as he used the Holy Grail, he could first weaken ninety percent of the opponent’s combat strength.
Even if it were Daniel himself, he would find that difficult to withstand, let alone others!

[Ding! You have killed demi-sage Garel. You have obtained Origin Crystal ×2,555 cubic units and the Divine-grade secret art Heavenly Illusion Art... Detected that you have sold this item. Millionfold Boost triggered! You have obtained Origin Crystal ×2.555 billion cubic units and the Sacred Art Illusory Dream Codex!]

[Ding! You have killed demi-sage Adonis. You have obtained Origin Crystal ×5,000 cubic units and the Divine-grade treasure Divine Source Orb (Sacred Artisan Law Grade)... However, the Law Essence was about to mature, and absorbing treasures required time. It was not convenient to inspect them carefully right now.
He casually put away the spoils and turned his gaze back toward the gray water lily, anticipation flickering in his eyes.
At this moment,
That gray water lily was undergoing an intense transformation.
The mist-like Chaotic Essence churned like boiling spring water, rushing eagerly into the petals of the Gray Lotus.
The color of the lotus became darker and more profound, like a dark star refined from chaos itself.
At the same time, the seven-colored light surrounding the water lily suddenly blazed brightly, burning like flames.
A mysterious and indescribable voice of the world rang out from somewhere unknown, echoing softly through the void like the whispers of ancient gods beside one’s ear.
"The voice of the world! And those are... Law fragments scattering outward..."
Daniel stared fixedly at the changes taking place in the Gray Lotus before him, the maturing lotus reflected in his pupils.
"The Law Essence is about to mature!"
System prompts rang beside his ears.
[Ding! You have received the baptism of the voice of the world. You have obtained divine energy +100,000 points!]
[Ding! You have received the baptism of the voice of the world. You have obtained divine energy +100,000 points!]

Just the baptism of the voice of the world that came with this Law Essence was already comparable to the gains from an Oracle-grade being personally expounding the mysteries.
The Astral Realm was truly worthy of being a miraculous land filled with opportunities everywhere!
"Law fragments. These are even better things!"
He stretched out his hand, and his palm transformed into a heaven-covering giant hand in the void.
"Celestial Grasp—!"
Whoosh—!
The giant hand descended like a curtain of heaven, gathering all the scattered seven-colored light into its palm.
This Sacred Art already possessed the property of storing all things, and now it was put to perfect use.

Daniel was pleasantly surprised.
Under the dual baptism of Law fragments and the voice of the world, his divine energy continued to surge wildly, instantly breaking through the one hundred billion mark!
And it was still continuing to climb, with no sign of stopping.
Buzz, buzz—!
At that moment, the petals of the Gray Lotus trembled slightly, releasing a soft rustling sound.
As it swayed, the surrounding space was actually torn open by force, revealing the pitch-black chaotic currents behind it, like cracks leading into an abyss.
The Gray Lotus wobbled in midair, like an infant clumsily yet stubbornly trying to take its first step.
"Hmm? This is... it has developed a will?"
"No! This Law Essence wants to escape!"
A sharp light burst from Daniel’s eyes.
"Dream on!"
Whoosh—!
The giant hand appeared once again, its five fingers opening as it grabbed toward the Law Essence that was trying to flee.
The Gray Lotus sensed a deadly crisis and desperately twisted its petals, attempting to tear space apart and escape into the chaotic currents.
But it had only just been born and was as ignorant as an infant.
How could it possibly escape Daniel’s palm?
Buzz—!
The giant hand firmly grabbed the Law Essence, its five fingers tightening and drawing it into the layered spaces of the world within his palm.
The gray water lily struggled a few times in his palm before finally quieting down.
[Ding! You have obtained Law Essence (Primordial Law Grade)!]

chapters.title: Chapter 340 -340-Eternal Sage, The World Beyond the Door
paragraphs: [Ding! You have obtained Law Essence (Primordial Law Grade)!]
It was actually a Primordial Law Grade essence!
Daniel was overjoyed. His mind power immediately sank into the world within his palm, wanting to examine the details of that Law Essence.

"The higher the quality of a Holy Relic, the better its effect when constructing a sage rank. I wonder how much help this Primordial Law Grade Law Essence will provide in forging a supreme sage rank?"
His mind power instantly saw the essence shaped like a Gray Lotus.
Its lotus petals were layered upon one another,幽光 flowing across them, as though it contained infinite mysteries.
[Law Essence · Reincarnation (Primordial Law Grade)]
Type: Special Holy Relic
Law: Reincarnation Law (high-grade)
Effect: Can be applied to any item, sage rank, Sacred Art, and more, granting the target the power of reincarnation.

Description: This is a Reincarnation Law Essence derived from the entanglement of Origin Laws. It can trap a target in an endless state of reincarnation. Unless one possesses Laws of the same level, a Primordial Law Grade Divine-grade treasure, or strength above the peak of Divine-grade, it cannot be broken.

Introduction: It was born in the depths of chaos before heaven and earth had yet been divided. It was nurtured, intertwined, and condensed by the Laws themselves, like a miraculous flower accidentally blooming within the starsea. Such a thing is nearly impossible to find in the world!
Daniel carefully finished reading the details.
"This Law Essence just happens to be perfectly compatible with my Divine Domain, Chaotic Reincarnation."
The corner of his mouth curved upward, and a sharp light flashed in his eyes.

"Moreover, I’ve already obtained the sage rank secret codex and have the freedom to choose a sage rank template. If I collect more top-tier Holy Relics now, along with enough divine energy, I’ll be able to construct a Divine-grade template and ascend to sage rank in one step!"
His chest rose and fell.
Once he advanced to sage rank...
The mission rewards, those final two elemental cores, would also be in his hands. Then he could unseal the Chronoverse Prologue Codex and grasp the Laws of spacetime!
"How exciting."
Endless Starsea, beyond the Sea of Chaos.
This place had neither form nor substance. It was like the primordial void before the universe had been opened, and even time itself seemed to have stopped flowing here.
Within the Sea of Chaos stood a mountain.
That mountain was exceedingly strange.
Looking upon it, there was nothing in sight except the mountain itself, as though the entire world existed solely for its sake.
Whoosh! Whoosh!
An old man and a young man appeared silently on the mountaintop.
The old man’s face was covered in wrinkles, like bark dried by the passage of time.
The young man had handsome brows and clear features, but his eyes were as deep as an abyss.
The old man and the young man walked side by side, like two stone statues that had come from ancient times.
"Synros has walked out of the Tomb of True Knowledge."
The young man’s voice was calm, like wind passing through an empty hall.
"In this forgotten corner of the starsea, countless eras have passed like flowing water, and he is the first being to walk out of that slumbering Tomb of True Knowledge."

"The fact that he could cross that tomb which devoured countless powerhouses means he has already stepped into the hall of the Eternal Sages—a threshold that countless great Oracle-grade beings could never touch even after exhausting their entire lives."
When the old man smiled, his face looked like a cracked riverbed.
He asked softly,
"But why did he choose this particular point in spacetime?"

"An Eternal Sage can roam freely through the Time River. Whether it is the dawn when the ancient stars first ignited, or the twilight in the distant future when the gods wither away, he deliberately came here."
"Because of Kelly."
The young man’s eyes flickered, and a meaningful smile rose at the corner of his mouth.
"We all know very clearly that Kelly’s only flaw exists in this spacetime."

"Everyone understands this, but everyone has remained still. No one is willing to be the reckless fool who steps into the trap first. This game has already been laid out on the chessboard of fate for a very, very long time."
"Kelly has never been able to cross that threshold and step into the hall of the supreme Divine-grade realm. Now, she has already become the focus of countless Eternal Sages!"
The old man sighed. Wrapped within that sigh were traces of regret and fear.

"Synros is truly worthy of being a supreme great Oracle-grade who dominated countless eras. He has only just entered the eternal level, yet his appetite is already so great. Although many Eternal Sages long to descend into the current spacetime, because Kelly exists here, no one dares act recklessly."
"But Synros is different... Is he not afraid that one wrong step will doom him beyond redemption?"
"No one dares underestimate Kelly."
A trace of fear flashed through the young man’s eyes.

"As one of the oldest Eternal Sages, Kelly is like a bottomless swamp. You think you have stepped on solid ground, but in the next instant, you may be swallowed whole. Those old monsters who have lived for far too long are none of them simple. Kelly is especially so."
"But her Mental State has never been perfected. It seems she will never be able to knock open the gate to that supreme Rank."
The old man’s smile carried a hint of schadenfreude.
"Eternity is like a sword hanging overhead, about to fall. What if Kelly..."
"No one can say for certain what Kelly’s eternal tribulation will be."
The young man cast his gaze toward the endless chaos, as though trying to see through the truth hidden behind that void.

"However, regarding Synros, I have obtained a small piece of information. He has already returned to his homeland in the current spacetime and is sharpening his blade, preparing to make a move against the Chaosverse."
"Oh?"
The old man’s eyes instantly lit up.
"He wants to dominate the Chaosverse of the current spacetime? That is no easy bone to chew!"
"Otherwise, he wouldn’t be Synros."
A playful curve rose at the corner of the young man’s mouth.

"In my opinion, once Synros starts making trouble, sooner or later he will drag all those eternal powerhouses into the vortex of the current spacetime. When that happens, this starsea that has been silent for so long may be swept into a storm of blood and slaughter."
Eternal Sages wandered within the Time River.
Their existence ran through the past and the future, scattered across different eras like stars.
Some dwelled in the ancient age when the starry sky first opened. Some lay dormant in the unimaginably distant future.
If an eternal powerhouse grew tired of the flow of time, they might even leap out of the Time River and wander aimlessly through the eternal void.
They would not easily appear at the same spacetime node unless some irresistible fate forcibly dragged them together.
"If Synros truly acts recklessly, he will indeed attract a large group of Eternal Sages."
The old man’s gaze was deep.
"It has been a very long time since I last saw such excitement. It seems that for a long time to come, we will not be bored..."
"This starry sky is finally about to burn once more."
The Door of Truth.
Simon said that after pushing it open, she might lose all her memories?
So, what should she choose?
Kelly hesitantly stretched out her hand and touched that cold, ancient Door of Truth.
Upon the door were engraved countless trajectories of stars and patterns of spacetime rifts, as though it sealed away the secrets of the entire universe.
Finally, at a certain moment, she used all her strength and pushed it open.
Boom—!
A deafening roar exploded beside her ears, like the collapse of the world.
Then, it stopped abruptly, falling into an eerie silence.
A faint warmth suddenly touched her face.
It was the warmth of sunlight.
The fragrance of flowers drifted on a warm breeze, lifting her hair like an invisible hand gently caressing it.
Ring, ring, ring...
An inexplicable bell suddenly rang.
At the same time, a deep voice sounded.
"Class dismissed."
Class dismissed?
Kelly opened her eyes.
Sunlight passed through the window, casting mottled patches across half of her face as light and shadow swayed.
"This is...?"

chapters.title: Chapter 341 -341-The Silhouette in Her Memories
paragraphs: Kelly’s gaze slowly swept across everything before her.
Walls interwoven with cream white and oak brown, a wide blackboard, rows of neatly arranged oak desks, and textbooks piled messily on top of them.
This place... was a classroom?
"Class is over, Kelly."
The girl sitting beside her spoke in a relaxed tone.
Kelly turned her head and glanced at her deskmate, then nodded silently.
However, questions churned in her mind.
Where is this?
Why have I appeared here?
What surprised her even more was that her memories had not disappeared!
Not only that, all kinds of common knowledge about this world, as well as the faces of her "family," had suddenly appeared in her mind out of nowhere...
What exactly did all of this mean?
Kelly silently pressed all her doubts deep into her heart.
Public Carriage No. 666 came to a steady stop at the station.
The students lined up and dropped copper coins into the carriage box one after another.
Kelly was still somewhat dazed.
The common knowledge and memories of "family" that had inexplicably surfaced in her mind made her feel faintly uneasy.
In a trance, she moved forward with the crowd, just like she had done countless times in her "memories."
At that moment, near the entrance of the carriage, the coachman suddenly shouted impatiently at a boy in front of him.
"In the name of the Seven Saints, hurry up and pay! Don’t hold up everyone behind you!"
"I... I’m terribly sorry."
The boy frantically searched through all his pockets, his expression growing more and more embarrassed.
"I... I forgot to bring money."
"Idiot! Why are you taking the carriage without money? Get down!"
The coachman waved his hand irritably.
The students lined up behind the boy also began shouting all at once.
"Daniel, hurry up and get down. Stop blocking our way!"
"Exactly! Hurry up and leave!"
"Don’t waste our time. My mom made mushroom cream soup tonight, and I’m already starving!"
The noisy complaints made Kelly frown.
Her gaze passed over the crowd and landed on the boy being driven away.
The boy named Daniel lowered his head and awkwardly stepped down from the carriage, his ears red as though they had been burned by fire.
Without saying a word, he walked along the street, not daring to turn back.
Kelly’s gaze fell on his retreating back...
Buzz—!!!
It was like lightning splitting open the silent night sky.
A thunderclap exploded deep within her soul.
Kelly trembled all over. The figure of that boy walking farther and farther away was reflected in her pupils, and for a long time, she could not look away.
That person...
Why does he look exactly like Brother Faustus?
"He is practically the same person."
"Please wait!"
Kelly suddenly spoke, urgency in her voice.
She could no longer suppress the emotions surging in her chest. Ignoring the gazes of the students around her, she quickly chased after him.
Daniel turned around blankly, her reflection appearing in his clear eyes.
Kelly walked up to him. A faint, unknown floral fragrance brushed past his nose.
"This classmate, I happen to have some spare money on me. I can lend it to you first."
Kelly took several copper coins out of her pocket and stared deeply into Daniel’s eyes, as though she wanted to look into the depths of his soul.
"You can pay me back later."
Warmth rose in Daniel’s heart. His throat bobbed slightly as he accepted the coins that still carried the warmth of her body.
"Thank you."
He raised his head and said seriously,
"My name is Daniel. I’m a third-year high school student. I’ll definitely pay this money back."
"My name is Kelly."
She smiled faintly. Her smile was gentle and bright.
"What a coincidence. I’m also in my third year."
Kelly returned to the place called "home."
In this world, "she" had only one relative—
Her maternal grandmother.
Her grandmother was already over seventy years old, with silver hair and hands covered in calluses.
She relied on collecting waste and a meager relief fund to support Kelly’s schooling.
And Kelly, in this world, also did whatever she could to ease her grandmother’s burden.
Every day after school, she would go to a restaurant run by their neighbor to do odd jobs and wash dishes. Her hands were often soaked until they turned pale.
At school, during lunch break.
Growl...
Daniel’s stomach cried out helplessly, sounding especially clear in the quiet classroom.
"I’ve been getting hungry faster and faster lately."
He endured the hunger in his stomach, his fingers gripping his pen tightly.
He was at an age when his body was growing, so he needed to eat more.
In the past, he could barely make it through the day with only breakfast and dinner. But now, that was no longer enough.
The afternoon was far too long. Every minute felt as though it had been stretched ten times over.
"Only studying can change the fate of poverty..."
He bit down hard on his lower lip. The taste of blood was salty and bitter.
"I don’t want to live in the dust forever. I want to rise above this."
Daniel was an orphan.
Just being able to attend high school had already taken everything he had.
But in his heart, an undying flame had always burned.
Suddenly, a familiar floral scent drifted into his nose.
It was Kelly’s scent.
"Daniel."
Kelly’s voice sounded beside his ear, pleasant like wind chimes.
"I brought a little too much lunch today, and I can’t finish it alone. Could you help me eat some? It would be such a waste otherwise."
Kelly had deliberately asked around about Daniel’s situation and learned that he was an orphan, and that his life was even harder than hers.
Before Daniel could nod, she had already opened the lunchbox.
It was part of the payment she had received from the restaurant where she worked. She had been reluctant to eat it herself and had carefully brought it to school.
"Bread, milk, and a chicken drumstick."
The rich fragrance drifting out of the lunchbox made Daniel, who was already unbearably hungry, swallow repeatedly.
"Thank you, Kelly."
He accepted the lunchbox, and warmth once again surged through his heart.
Under Kelly’s deliberate approach, Daniel gradually came to like her.
School life had originally been a tunnel with no end in sight.
But in their eyes, that period of time was so brief it seemed to pass in the blink of an eye.
Their weary youth passed in an instant.
By the riverside, the river stretched endlessly, and the setting sun dyed the water golden.
Daniel held Kelly’s hand as they walked in the river breeze. The gravel beneath their feet made soft, crisp sounds.
"I’m leaving tomorrow to work in Nurentin, Kelly."
He watched the river water wash over the backs of his feet, the cool sensation bringing a moment of comfort.
"Once I save enough tuition, I’ll be able to go directly to Nurentin University."
He paused, then turned his head to look at her.
"Kelly, Starlight University has already accepted you. When are you going?"
Kelly smiled and shook her head, her eyes filled with determination.
"The place I want to go isn’t Starlight."
"Oh? Where do you want to go?"
"Nurentin."
She lowered her head shyly, the tips of her ears turning slightly red.
"I want to go where you are!"
Daniel froze for a moment, then suddenly asked,
"Then what about Starlight..."
"I don’t want to go to university anymore. My grandmother is old. I need to earn money to support her and myself."
Kelly’s tone was calm, as though she were speaking of something insignificant.
"I also applied to Nurentin University, but..."
She suddenly laughed softly and lifted her head to look at him.
"You have to study properly, understood?"
"Mm."
Daniel blinked, and a smile rose at the corner of his mouth.
"After I graduate from university, let’s get married!"
Kelly’s eyes suddenly lit up, like fireworks blooming in the night sky.
"Who said I’m going to marry you?"
She turned her face away, pretending to look toward the distant river. But her voice was as soft as a mosquito’s buzz.
"What kind of beautiful dream are you having?"

This place... was a classroom?
"Class is over, Kelly."
The girl sitting beside her spoke in a relaxed tone.
Kelly turned her head and glanced at her deskmate, then nodded silently.

Where is this?
Why have I appeared here?

What exactly did all of this mean?
Kelly silently pressed all her doubts deep into her heart.
Public Carriage No.
666 came to a steady stop at the station.
The students lined up and dropped copper coins into the carriage box one after another.
Kelly was still somewhat dazed.
The common knowledge and memories of "family" that had inexplicably surfaced in her mind made her feel faintly uneasy.
In a trance, she moved forward with the crowd, just like she had done countless times in her "memories."

I’m terribly sorry."

I forgot to bring money."

Why are you taking the carriage without money?
Get down!"
The coachman waved his hand irritably.
The students lined up behind the boy also began shouting all at once.
"Daniel, hurry up and get down.

"Exactly!
Hurry up and leave!"
"Don’t waste our time.
My mom made mushroom cream soup tonight, and I’m already starving!"

Her gaze passed over the crowd and landed on the boy being driven away.
The boy named Daniel lowered his head and awkwardly stepped down from the carriage, his ears red as though they had been burned by fire.

Kelly’s gaze fell on his retreating back...
Buzz—!!!

A thunderclap exploded deep within her soul.
Kelly trembled all over.

Kelly suddenly spoke, urgency in her voice.

chapters.title: Chapter 342 -342-An Angel Sent by God
paragraphs: Nurentin, a fast-food restaurant.
Daniel sat beneath the dim yellow light, counting the savings in his hand. Exhausted, he rubbed his sore eyes.
"The tuition is enough, but I’m still short on living expenses."
Hearing this, Kelly immediately rummaged through her bag and pulled out a stack of bills.
"I saved five thousand over the past three months of work. Take it all."
She stuffed the money into his hand, her tone leaving no room for refusal.
"You know my shop provides food and lodging. Use this first."
"Five thousand? Your monthly wage is only two thousand..."
Daniel’s eyes widened in surprise.
Kelly proudly lifted her chin, her smile carrying a hint of playfulness.
"That’s nothing. If not for some necessary expenses, I could have saved even more. Next month, I can save nineteen hundred."
"But your grandmother..."
Daniel frowned slightly.
Kelly froze for a moment, then spoke in a relaxed tone.
"It’s a small problem. I can ask my boss for an advance on my wages. Your schooling is more important."
Daniel quietly looked at her.
It was as though he had returned to that starving noon in high school, to the moment she had walked over with a lunchbox.
Kelly truly seemed like an angel sent by God to save him.
"Thank you, Kelly."
His voice was a little choked.
"You must wait for me to graduate."
Kelly’s ears were already completely red.
She lowered her head and replied softly,
"Okay."
On that very day,
Her grandmother fell seriously ill and was sent to the intensive care unit.
Kelly wanted to go, only to discover that she could not even scrape together the fare.
The surgery fee was an astronomical sum.
She gritted her teeth, her nails digging into her palm.
"I can’t let Daniel worry. I can handle this."
She had once heard Aunt Carly next door mention a place where one could exchange blood for money...
At the blood station.
Kelly timidly walked through the cold glass doors and found the staff member behind the counter.
"Excuse me..."
Her hands clutched the hem of her clothes.
"How much money can I get for selling blood?"
The staff member raised his head and looked at the sallow-faced young girl before him.
He wanted to say, You’re still young and malnourished. Go home and take better care of yourself before coming back.
But then he thought again.
If she had not reached the end of her rope, why would a teenage girl ever step into a place like this?
He sighed, his eyes carrying a trace of pity.
"Little girl, I hope this is the last time you ever appear here."
Several years later, at dusk.
An apartment in the city.
Click!
The sound of a key turning came from outside the door, and Kelly jumped up cheerfully.
Daniel pushed the door open and entered, his expression dazed, as though he had just awakened from a nightmare.
"What’s wrong? Did something go wrong with the exam?"
The excitement on Kelly’s face instantly vanished, replaced by deep worry.
"My investment failed. The product’s reception was mediocre. I lost everything!"
Daniel hugged Kelly tightly, his voice choked.
"Kelly, am I a complete bastard? I lost every cent we saved over all these years."
Tears burst from his eyes and slid down his cheeks.
"I wanted to wait until I graduated next year and give you a proper wedding... But now..."
"It’s okay..."
Kelly gently patted his head, as though comforting an injured child.
"It’s all right. I’ve also saved some money over the years. There should be a little over a hundred thousand..."
"What!"
Daniel suddenly raised his head, light bursting from his eyes.
"Give it all to me! I’ll definitely win back everything we lost!"
Kelly looked into those burning eyes and nodded heavily.
"Okay. I’ll give it all to you!"
"I believe in you!"
One year later.
It was still that same apartment.
Daniel was decorating the place for the wedding, bustling around the home.
Kelly brought steaming dishes out from the kitchen and set the bowls and chopsticks.
"Dinner’s ready."
Her voice was like birdsong in the morning.
"Coming, my dear."
Daniel walked over and sat down. Looking at the two simple dishes before him, his face bloomed with a smile.
"They look wonderful."
"Go wash your hands."
Kelly rolled her eyes at him, though that gaze was filled with sweetness.
"As you command, my Kelly."
Daniel walked briskly toward the sink.
The two sat down.
Daniel picked up his spoon and was just about to start eating.
"Wait."
Kelly suddenly took out two brand-new spoons from beside her.
"I bought two new spoons. On a special day like today, there should at least be something new. We can’t afford anything else, but we can still afford spoons."
Daniel smiled and accepted the spoon.
He scooped up some food and stuffed it into his mouth, speaking unclearly as he chewed.
"My dear, your cooking is truly a delicacy of this world."
"I wish I could eat it every single day!"
Kelly smiled, happiness filling even the fine lines at the corners of her eyes.
"Then, Mr. Daniel, please eat more. And today, there is wine too."
She poured two glasses of wine, the pale golden liquid swaying gently in the cups.
The two raised their glasses at the same time and lightly clinked them together in the air, producing a crisp sound.
"Mr. Daniel, happy wedding."
Kelly smiled, starlight flickering in her eyes.
"Mrs. Kelly, happy wedding."
Daniel’s voice was somewhat choked, and tears slid down his face despite himself.
Daniel was meticulously straightening the dark suit he wore.
It was a precious suit of armor Kelly had found at a secondhand stall and ironed flat overnight.
Even the slightest wrinkle had to be smoothed out by force, as though he were a knight polishing his armor before battle.
Kelly walked to his side and handed him the briefcase.
"It’s your first interview. Don’t be too nervous."
Kelly smiled, her eyes filled with warm and unwavering trust.
"You will always be the sharpest sword in my heart. May the stars crown your steps."
"My dear, just wait at home for my good news!"
Daniel bent down and kissed her forehead. Then he turned and stepped across the threshold.
Behind him was the earnest gaze of his beloved.
The company Daniel had applied to was called Nurentin International, one of the most powerful multinational conglomerates on the continent.
With his impressive academic background and outstanding abilities, he successfully obtained an employment contract.
As he walked out of the interview hall, he met the previous interviewee head-on.

She was an elite student who had returned from overseas. Her bearing was elegant, and every gesture carried an innate nobility, like the daughter of an aristocrat who had stepped out of an ancient painting.
"Good day. My name is Yvette Klein."
She extended her hand with a proper and generous smile.
"I heard you also passed the interview. From now on, we will be colleagues. Which department will you be joining, sir?"
Daniel said calmly,
"The Business Department."
"What a marvelous coincidence. So am I."
Yvette’s gaze lingered on his face for an extra moment before she extended her fair hand.
"I hope we can look after each other from now on. It will be a pleasure working with you."
Daniel glanced at her hand but did not take it. He merely bowed slightly.
"My apologies. I must return immediately to tell my wife this good news. Please forgive me."
Yvette watched Daniel’s departing back, an unusual light rising in her eyes.
He rejected me?
The corner of her mouth lifted slightly.
At this moment, the desire to conquer him quietly sprouted in her heart like wild grass.
"Daniel..."
She softly murmured his name.

chapters.title: Chapter 343 -343-The Choice of a Smart Person
paragraphs: The city apartment.
"Kelly, I did it! I got accepted!"
Daniel pushed the door open and could not wait to tell Kelly the good news.
Kelly burst into tears of joy, her vision blurring.
She choked out,
"You did it!"
"From the very first moment I met you, I knew that no chains could ever bind your wings."
Daniel smiled and pulled her into his arms.

"Kelly, once I make something of myself, we’ll move into a bigger house. It’ll face the sea. We’ll be able to hear the waves singing as they strike the reefs, and see the first flower of spring bloom before the window."
"Mm!"
Kelly nodded heavily. Tears were still flowing, yet the corners of her mouth had already curved into a crescent moon.
"However, I need to go to the company headquarters for a six-month internship. After six months, I’ll return to your side."
"I’ll stay here and wait for your return."
Kelly paused, then asked worriedly,
"But... do you still have enough money?"
Daniel gave a bitter smile, his eyes filled with helplessness and self-reproach.
"Don’t worry. Take all the money at home with you. I’ll take good care of myself."
Kelly spoke gently, without the slightest hesitation in her voice.
The day after Daniel left, Kelly quit her original job.
Because that job took up too much of her time.
She wanted to take on more part-time jobs and turn every minute into shining bills.
During the day, she worked as a server at a church, carrying plates, pouring water, and greeting people with a smile.
As dusk approached, she shuttled through streets and alleys, delivering steaming meal boxes to strangers’ doors.
Late at night, she worked as a waitress in a tavern, cleaning cups and plates amid the noise of voices and the smell of alcohol.
Three part-time jobs in a single day.
She was like a tireless spinning top, turning beneath the whip of fate.
"With all three jobs together, I can probably make eight or nine thousand a month. I should be able to save over eight thousand."
Kelly calculated silently in her heart, remembering every account clearly.
"Daniel is an employee of a big company now. I can’t let his coworkers look down on him. I need to buy him a few decent sets of clothes."
"He probably won’t eat well out there either. And there are those social gatherings with colleagues... How can a man manage outside if his pockets are empty?"
"If I’m frugal, a few hundred should be enough for me. I’ll send him the rest."
Half a year passed quietly, leaving no trace behind.
Because of his outstanding performance, Daniel received a company award.
Yvette was also among those awarded!
Because they had spent half a year together on a business trip at headquarters, the two of them had already become as familiar as old friends.
Nurentin Airport.
"Daniel, a car will be coming to pick me up in a moment. Shall I give you a ride?"
A trace of expectation that was difficult to detect hid in Yvette’s gaze.
"Thank you for your kindness, but my wife will be coming to pick me up. There’s no need to trouble yourself."
Daniel politely declined, his tone courteous yet distant.
"Oh? The airport is so far from the city, yet your wife is personally driving here to pick you up?"
Yvette’s eyes flickered, and she was secretly surprised.
As the two spoke, a black luxury sedan slowly stopped by the roadside, its body reflecting a cold gleam beneath the sunlight.
A driver wearing white gloves respectfully opened the door.
"Miss, please get in."
Yvette was unwilling to give up and asked for the third time,
"Are you sure you don’t need a ride?"
Daniel was just about to speak when he suddenly saw a battered little electric scooter hurriedly approaching from the distance.
The figure on the scooter trembled slightly in the cold wind, like a stubborn withered leaf refusing to fall.
"No need. My wife has already arrived."
Warmth suddenly entered his voice.
Yvette followed his gaze and saw that simple little scooter. An indescribable shock rose in her heart.

Daniel and Kelly embraced tightly, as though they had been separated for an entire century, and yet as though they had never parted at all.
"Get on."
Daniel climbed onto the little electric scooter and motioned for Kelly to sit behind him.
"Mm!"
Kelly wrapped both arms around his waist, pressing her cheek against his broad back.
The cold wind cut across their faces, icy and biting.
But in both their chests, a fire was burning, warm and bright.
Within that cold wind, there seemed to be a honey-like sweetness that seeped into the heart.
Nurentin Company.
